Cons: From 2010 to 2015, Ginny the CEO inherited an aggressive profit target that was unachievable as the company did not realize Revenue growth. It took a bit long for the leadership team to realize it and adjust, but hopefuly they will realize growth again soon. The focus on Acquisitions is necessary but Mergers should be considered as well to move the top line more aggressively.

Pros: work with very smart and professional people  benefits 401K, medical, life insurance, vac. But, new hire quality of benefits is not as robust  constant challenging environment  most teammates/employees are very helpful  management is usually very well trained and effective  treated with respect and diverse workforce  salary raises are now market based and seem more fair  no bias found in salary levels between male and female  equal pay has been a protocol since the company was founded  love the opportunity to work remotely  has some great community programs   the company business conduct guidelines and values to work by are stellar
Cons: lack of communication from director level and above  only aware of happenings in our own org  high pressure environment  lack of job security  anyone can be laid off resourced at any time  constant lay offs as products/technology evolves/changes  overtime my benefits have been reduced. The 401k match used be paid to you throughout the year, now it is paid in last paycheck of the year and if you separate you don't get that years match.  work long hours @ end of quarters

Pros: Some of the brightest people that I've ever worked with work at IBM.  IBM has invented a number of significant, important parts of the Information Technology industry.  This includes relational database technology and hard disk drive technology.  IBM is one of the few companies that actually performs the "Research" portion of "Research and Development".
Cons: Like many large companies, IBM is laden with bureaucracy and often inane procedure.  Also, it is completely beyond understanding why a company that has reported record earnings, record profits and has a positive outlook for 2009 would  one day after it's proclamation to the financial community  commence laying off 5,000 of its employees, most of whom were real contributors to the company's success.  IBM's approach to this latest round of layoffs was very calculating, ensuring that no single location was affected in a significant enough way to require additional notice or pay.

Pros: Having IBM on your resume gets attention.  Working at IBM means you don't have to explain what company you work for.  Vendors call you back, and you can push an escalation if need be.  The biggest advantage of working at IBM is the vastness of the company.  You can go as high as you want to  maybe.  There are endless training opportunities and lots of things to do.
Cons: IBM periodically goes through an exercise called a "Resource Action" or "RA," which of course is a euphemism for a layoff.  That is how I parted ways with the company.  The company is gradually reducing its US workforce while increasing its staffing in India and China.  Effects on morale are what you'd expect.

Pros: In my position there are no tight deadlines to speak of.  Pretty laid back.  Plenty of work to keep my busy, but not a lot of pressure to meet hard deadlines.  I come from just the opposite so it's a huge difference for me.
Cons: Lotus Notes is terrible... I feel like it is the mid 90's.  It's slow and buggy... I honestly could not stand using it if I was in my previous high pressure and high email volume job... Since my role at IBM is pretty laid back  the lost productivity just means I get less done... but that's OK.          Required use of Linux as a desktop for anyone with privileged access.   I like Linux as a server and like the command line but hate it for desktop OS.    Things can be slow to happen... like getting access to things or policy changes... etc...

Pros: Simply put, you will be working with a range of professionals who are smart, passionate and either wellrespected for their subject matter expertise or the promise of their future potential   It is a culture that demands high performance which ensures everyone is bringing their best effort, especially in light of a highly matrix, virtual workforce.  There is solidarity and a very strong emotional connection to understanding the saying of "once an IBMer, always an IBMer"  It has always been an organization that could reinvent itself
Cons: In the last 10 years, it is an organization that has lost its way, most noticeably on what it means  to have an engaged and empowered workforce.    While it is essential for organisations to change, IBM has failed to do this with a higher degree of emotional intelligence and organizational savvyness.   Its greatest asset is its workforce and yet they've become the most embattled

Pros: From day one, I have had a sense that I would be provided every opportunity to succeed. I would be provided the tools and resources to do so. What is communicated from our  organization's VP down, is an expectation to excel at your work, to work hard, and understand that family is first. This type of communication to a large degree, alleviates the family/ work conflict.  In other words, because I am "allowed" to prioritize my family, I don't mind staying late, working early to excel at my work. Flexibility within reason has allowed me to take care of doctors appointments, work from home with sick kids, and still excel and communicate my commitment to the company.
Cons: I've started IBM as they have gone away from trend they started; working from home! We have employees that for the past 15 years, have worked from home. I never had the opportunity to do so, but for some of my co workers it has been a tremendous lifestyle adjustment. But such is life. This is the closes thing to a con that I could come up with !

Pros: If you luck out with a good management chain then I can see why folks stay in this role for their entire career, but it's unlikely. You can create your own schedule so worklife balance is super flexible as long as your closing deals. I like how we are market segmented, so I only work with customers in a particular industry. Great for providing similar market use cases between customers. Travel was abundant prior to COVID which made the job worth it.
Cons: Number driven, Executives are not supportive, not great culture. I feel alone a lot when it comes to getting help or support from a management level.

Pros: Really great benefits: medical insurance is great, college hires get 15 days vacation off the bat, they have a wellness program to follow where they give you a rebate, worklife balance is determined by you you can choose to work only 40 hr a week or you can choose to work more.  Wonderful to have a Big 5 company on your resume.  Higher salary over many other companies when starting as a college hire.
Cons: They have great benefits when getting hired out of college, but they do a poor job of teaching college hires the ropes. IBM will place a young cheap college hire anywhere and expect them to know the business process/area. There's not much room to grow as a college hire and not much choice on project, you're basically just placed into a position if you have little experience. Even they've said it, you're a body that is charging the client and making a profit for them.  Raises are extremely small, bonuses are rare. They try to cut back to make more profit for themselves and don't reward their 'minions' for the work they do.

Pros: For those afforded the opportunity to work from home, there is great work/life balance.  The company does have some decent benefits, though healthcare benefits have waned dramatically over the past few years.  The biggest benefit of working in a company like IBM, however, is the ability to move into different roles and try new things. The company is vast, and opportunities abound.
Cons: I've worked at IBM for many years.  The culture has shifted dramatically, and not all for the good.  The executives clearly don't care much about the individual employee and are focused, quarter to quarter, on the stockholders only.  They have yet to realize that treating the employees well will result in better results, better profitability.  The shift to "colocation" within the past couple of years has done a lot of damage to morale, even for those not directly impacted.

Pros: Good breath of technology Decent benefits
Cons: IBM has ZERO loyalty to its employees, particularly in the US. Work goes offshore > fire US employee Cheaper out of college resource available > fire US employee  Also, as documented in various lawsuits and industry articles, if you are over 40, there is a target in your head. You work hard, and get good reviews throughout your career, so that you reach a decent salary band. Great, right? Wrong. Because now you are too expensive for IBM to make a good profit margin, so you are a top candidate for one of the many Resource Actions. That's when there is an arbitrary order from the top for managers to cut a certain percentage of people above a certain band.  For the record, I'm still employed by IBM, and managed to survive many rounds of cuts. But I have absolutely no illusions that my job is safe.  If you are young and need a relatively low starting salary, IBM is probably hiring across all fronts.  So you can make a quick buck. But if you're interested in starting at a company where you can grow, look elsewhere.

Pros: Nonsalary benefits are good time off, insurance, 401k, etc  Good learning experience for the fundamentals of a data center  Job security if you know what you are doing, you're pretty safe because they literally can not afford to fire you due to staffing issues even if you messup  Free snacks
Cons: Overworked and constantly understaffed  High turnover rate  Management anyone above the site manager is a writeoff, your local site manager can be hit or miss  Uncompetitive salary  Outside of Dallas, your ability to move into other IBM Cloud IaaS teams like network or compute is nonexistent

Pros: The worldrenowned sales training that you get during the Summit Program far exceeds other top companies.  There is a mix of executive speakers, classroom sales training, abundant live sales training with experienced IBM sellers, technology training, and professional advice that really prepares you for a career in professional consultative sales.  Beyond just the training, there is a great opportunity to network with peers in the Summit program as well as IBMers outside of the program.  The networking is a huge benefit from a personal friendship and a professional standpoint.  Much of the training takes place in cities around the country, so there is an opportunity to work remotely.  I have only been in the Summit Program for a few months, but I am already very impressed.  I know multiple IBMers that have graduated from the Summit Program and have been very successful.  I am proud to be part of this great program and great company.
Cons: IBM is a large company, which has its advantages/disadvantages.  One disadvantage is that there is plenty of administrative work that has to be done, but that is common with many professional roles.

Pros: Always new technology and ideas to work on.  You can do pretty much whatever you want, learn whatever you want  as long as you make money for the company.  You can have a long career in various roles within the company.  Very flexible work/life  lots of remote workers.
Cons: In the last couple years, IBM has been doing tons of layoffs.  They are chopping here and there, whatever is needed to make the quarterly earnings report look good.  They have lost a lot of great people.  At the same time, they are hiring people like mad too.  There are constant reorgs.  Don't be surprised if your manager changes every year.  And perhaps the name of your organization too.  You can do fine there.. but you could get randomly hit too.  Just be careful and always be prepared.

Pros: Great benefits and training  IBM never really looks bad on your resume
Cons: Pay  If you are a motivated and industrious hard worker, you are better off elsewhere. Socialized earnings  top and bottom not much difference. Better have a manager who will fight for your commissions. I continually blew out my quota but was given retroactive quota increases  that resulted in negative commission checks! Yes  I am being serious. Explanation: "Since you do so well and were paid in the bonus in the previous quarter, with the increased quota, you were actually overpaid ... so you owe us money." They never made you pay it and tried to make it sound like you were being done a favor when it was 'wiped clean' at the beginning of the next year. Net net  they fund you not off the dollars you sell but at a percentage of your salary. Go someplace that pays you for what you actually sell at a guaranteed rate.

Pros: A dynamic and flexible work environment that allows for an intrapreneurial approach to managing internal and external IBM customers. A wealth of talent to draw and learn from. Excellent continuing training and educational benefits.
Cons: IBM is not a work environment for nonselfstarters as employees are expected to have high business and personal standards; business expectations and customer satisfaction run high so employees must be diligent and innovative. While many may find this as a "Con", I found it to be highly motivational; who doesn't want to be on a team determined to win? IBM plays to win  so do I! You will need to if you want to exceed expectations and receive real rewards.

Job Title: Customer Engineer Ii In San Jose, Ca: (Past Employee - 2009)
Pros: Pros customer engineer work is fun & customers are glad to see you.  a breadth of stores and banks means you do not get bored.
Cons: Cons emphasis on numbers, quantity not quality. management expects things to get fixed, with no regards to time/distance,manpower resources, support, training, parts needed. they expect you to meet 3 numbers 86%: a/ get to the site within 1/2 hrs. b/get it fixed now/today. c/numbers of stores min 5 a day my territory was 2hrs long & 1 hr wide. I spend average 3 hrs driving a day, and still be expected to meet numbers. management is nut: one day i was told to work til you drop respond to ATM service 7/24/365, next day "no OT without approval from manager" company release shoddy/unreliable machinery check processing module to bank of america, without any training to field service engineers. Then months later were forced to send them to training only when we have to revisit the same machine twice a day because engineers don't know how to fix

Pros: Large organization that you can move around and find different opportunities. Innovative company with leading edge or first of a kind technology solutions. Corporate Services Corp Leadership Program.
Cons: Eliminating vast majority of US resources for cheaper off shore labor. Can be a top performer with all the accolades possible and still be let go in order to be replaced with cheaper labor off shore, which is the path the company continues to do. Working remotely is now much more rare as most employees have to be colocated in only one of handful of cities in the US. Poor HR management structure. You are typically on your own as far as career development and have to strongly advocate for yourself even for things as simple as training. Very expensive health benefits especially if you have more than 1 child. Minimal bonus and raises even for top performers.

Pros: Decent bonus structure if they give it to you. If you’re in good with upper management the sky is the limit. If they are gone or move on you have to start again. Be aware of this and know your second and third plus line bosses and your journey is fulfilling.
Cons: There’s no rhyme or reason to the layoffs. In February of my last year as a technical person I made a 90k bonus responsible for large sales. One month later told my position no longer needed. The funny thing is they would keep continue to hire people for the same role that was going away.  Everything about IBM is now a who you know up top to shield you. You lose your safety shield and you’re exposed. It’s dumb when you see worldwide experts let go, but those who are just buddy buddy with upper management are kept around when others do their role for them.

Pros: IBM leaders demonstrate integrity, fairness, appreciation, and enthusiasm You are appreciated for your ability to grow the company through learning Although IBM is "extreme" technical; your skills in learning, development, and facilitation are equally valued Project oriented work  you are a trusted professional  not 95; loads of work/life flexibility  Endless opportunities to be creative  develop new learning programs and see them through to delivery Lots of cool tools, very organized, clear communications Fun people to work with, fast paced
Cons: Always a possibility of layoffs IBM has a reputation of being slow and old You do all your own administrative work  no support  IBM is a big place, it's easy to get overwhelmed and you won't ever understand how the entire company works Managers are under a lot of pressure and have lots of red tape  sometimes their hands are tied in making decisions

Pros: As a second career professional, I have found that working at IBM has truly fulfilled my desire and goal to find the meaningful capstone of my professional journey. IBM is a company that encourages and fosters the growth and innovation of all in a very inclusive environment. From the support of management, to the highly collaborative and innovative culture, to the expansive array of learning paths, certification tracks, and learning resources, IBM provides the means for all to not only succeed in their current position, but to fully prepare themselves for success at the next level, and in reaching their full potential. I have found the work to be extraordinarily meaningful and fulfilling, such that I'm happy to go to work everyday, and proud to be an IBMer!
Cons: IBM is such a large global company that getting oriented can seem rather daunting and overwhelming. But with support of the management team and peers, and with some individual effort to network and learn, that downside is effectively eliminated.

Pros: the training for sales is the best in the business.  Strong team and IBM provided adequate time to take the training.  Sales compensation was average at best
Cons: lack of support  everything is "on your own" to figure out.  You get 5 page emails to set up your phone and no support if it doesn't work.  Hopefully you have a friend that can help you out Antiquated systems  the forecasting solution is a joke.  It's still Excel based, way too complicated, and you spend a great deal of time trying to figure out why numbers don't match no teamwork  there is no sense of team. none.  most of the team is made up of "B" and "C" players just trying to "get by" and find a role where they can "hide" for a year or two

Pros: few Professional and talented coworkers
Cons: Incompetent and Toxic Management, backstabbing  coworkers, employees are afraid to speak up, tyrannical leaders, obsolete and incompetent old managers 3040+ year with IBM that act as IBM henchmen. No career opportunities. If you ask for a transfer in another technology or organization even in the same location your performance review will be sabotage  to be "layoff" aka  Resource Action RA in the next round. No job security. You feel like a temp employee surviving every day until you are RAed or get a a job offer from another company  TO NEWLY  COLLEGE GRADUATE STAY AWAY FROM IBM. Its not the company to learn new technology or build a career.

Pros: It's a paycheck.  Nice to have the name on your resume. It explains you need to find a new place to work.
Cons: Not allowed to vary from the tasks for your job or risk breaking rules of lean management.  No meaningful career advancement options without working day shift and replacing your next immediate superior when and if they leave.  No realistic career track or mentoring available.  Productivity improvements are gained by heaping more and more work on fewer and fewer full time equivalent employees regardless of what the service level contracts promise customers.  Management meets its performance review targets by double booking man hours on multiple contracts resulting in inadequate staffing levels.  Rank order employees in performance reviews punish mistakes and job requirements leave no room for exceptional performance.  If you stick with this company and you’ll destroy your long term career path options.   Then you'll get an offer to retire early so they can hire a college grad for less than half of you salary.

Pros: Hardest problems to solve, you learn tons!; World class customers and the smartest people on the planet to work with.  Ability to move around to many new careers every 2 years.
Cons: NO LIFE, NO PAY, NO SENSE OF COMMUNITY, THREAT OF BEING FIRED EVERY DAY.  Constantly changing the compensation rules so they take away from you any profit and bonuses your hard work generated.  Most of it is simply unethical!!  It has become a mean and selfish culture which uses it "VALUES" only as a way to beat the employees while management does not live by any of them.  Travel rules have become so over burdensome and complex and just seem to be a way of making the employee pay for as much of the cost of doing IBM business as is legally possible.  NO ONE wants to travel for IBM unless you are a manager and are exempt from all this nonsense.

Pros: Schedule Flexibility, Benefits, Paid Expenses via no hassle Amex Card, corporate paid mobile, ability to travel around the world, great salary and bonus NOT soley in RSU's like most tech companies. I personally do not want to gamble on my bonus and future salary. great use of industry tools for communication and development, lots of free learning, not just IBM products
Cons: IBM is large with over 300k employees around the world, I can see how some might at first feel lost. Quiet introverts would have a hard time I think. Obviously this isnt a startup company so no startup excitement feel. Vacation time is low at the beginning. look past that, IBM is very flexible with time off.

Pros: Lots of training, looks great on a resume. Only useful as a stepping stone to a real career.
Cons: Poorly organized, incompetent workers and disinterested management. Salary is less than half the industry average for the position I held. Endless stream of lies about roles, raises, and travel obligations. Places client demands over legal obligations to the state and employees. incredibly unprofessional coworkers with minimal education and zero work ethic. Zero communication between management and employees regarding client engagements, etc.  Misleading hiring process most employees at our center were told they would be programming for mobile development, java, etc, but were instead trained on something entirely unrelated to their areas of interest.

Pros: I worked in the pharma industry for 25 years and felt that there was a strong organizational structure and very informed training and education developmental training strong enough to address physicians very intelligently. But nothing prepared me for the strength of IBM's Your Learning and there focus on continuous learning and upskilling. I wish all companies had the opportunity to prepare for their future with a focus on their people and the hot roles and hot skills of today and tomorrow.
Cons: Although IBM is a big behemoth of a company, there is significant effort by the organization to prepare leaders to lead and to make it feel more like a family and that we are in it together. The con is that, of course, is not portrayed by every leader at IBM.

Pros: 12 hour work shift means you only have to work 3 or 4 days a week. At least 2 weeks of paid vacation with the opportunity to earn more.
Cons: You have to work most major holidays including the 4th of July and Thanksgiving. They never have funds available for morale building events like they had in the past.  If you have issues with payroll you must call employee services where you are directed to a call center overseas. These employees have no real idea what's going, only a rouch black and white outline of what is suppose to happen. There is a HUGE disconnect between even the manager and payroll.   When you leave IBM it is very common for them to over pay you and then either take the money back straight from your bank account or send you a bill, threatning to send it to collections if you do not pay.  They hire, fire and layoff thousands of people every year... you would think they would get this right by now.

Pros: Good benefits, office life is rare as work from home is more common. Most of the real IBMers are simply  fantastic people to work with.
Cons: Wow, where to begin. L1L2 management are largely nothing more than puppets. I actually had a manager say they made a decision based on a coin flip. That sounds funny at first, but it really isn't. Worklife balance? What's that? I've missed numerous big family events for essentially nothing in return. Personal work reviews are a joke. HR gives first line a manager a bucket of numbers to assign their employees regardless what the team is really worth. Very few get what they actually earn. Roadkill 2015 is a huge moral killer because of all the layoffs actually mass unjustified firings is what they really are. Execs have finally gotten as corrupt as other big companies. Very sad what this great company is becoming. Watson is rolling over in his grave.

Pros: flexible work schedule. work with great people. great place for someone first getting in to IT.
Cons: It can get stressful, especially when you are left to deal with the customer, when it is supposed to be the job of the account team. They hire anyone who has touched a computer. I have been with IBM for 2 years. never saw a promotion, can't apply for other jobs in IBM because I'm a critical player in my team, but people who have to come to me for help on a constant basis are favored for promotions. for a company that thrives off of innovation, whenever I innovated something, it took a long time, and a lot of reaching out to dead ends to bring my ideas and innovations to life. it is defiantly a company that looks better from the outside, than it does from the inside.

Pros: The best part of working at IBM is it's people. They hire smart, passionate individuals, who help each other succeed. A growth mindset is crucial to have at IBM. You will learn so much about technology and each other!  It's easy to find side projects to grow your skills & portfolio, and you'll need to do that.
Cons: There is no real upward movement. Unfortunately due to the sheer amount of staff, management doesn't have proper headcount or allowance to allow for promotions. This means that more senior designers eventually leave for other organizations, or are removed with yearly layoffs.  Also, due to the kinds of work you do, you might not have anything in a portfolio to show for it. This is common knowledge among management, but no one in leadership roles attempts to fix this challenge, probably because they're overloaded elsewhere.

Pros: I worked for IBM for almost 30 years, through good times and bad. Loved it >90% of the time. The biggest pro to the company is your coworkers smart, creative, and fun. New CEO Arvind Krishna is a true pro, I had the pleasure of working under him for a number of years. Found him to be brilliant, and an excellent, fair manager. He's so good that as a retiree I have invested in IBM again. I expect him to lead IBM back to solid dominance in Quantum, Blockchain, and AI.
Cons: Cons are the occasional poor 1st line mgr, but that was rare during my long career. Another con was Finance/CFOled strategic decisionmaking rather than tech leaders and management. Too many buybacks, not enough R&D. That may change under Arvind.

Pros: Elevators,  good chairs, good lighting, nice view from upper floors,  nice lobby,  a little coffee nook to ponder ones escape.  It is in the nice little city of Dubuque.  IM
Cons: More dysfunctional than most large companies I have worked at.  Leadership provided  by "professional managers"  with no IT sense. If you enjoy changing & tracking your passwords youll like it here,  not 5 or 6,  like 40 constantly expiring. The 10 accounts you ll be supporting all have different configurations,  login procedures,  rules India coworkers are 12 hours away,  many that are difficult to understand. Prepare to give up all of your personal digits to anonymous requests from the many clients across the globe to secure your personal access to their data systems. Remember you will be fired if you share a id or password, understandable. High turnover,  depressing to see hope fade in the newbies.

Pros: With IBM for 25 years.....   I've seen IBM's leadership  transform to understand and advocate for LGBT rights in all countries.  There are countries and states, which do not have laws about rights for our community, and IBM has negotiated and educated some to understand the value our GLBT diversity brings to the market and spending power.  Last time I checked we had 42 Out Executives in IBM world wide, imagine that!
Cons: No matter where you are there are still people afraid and confused about our journey in life.

Pros: IBM's Summit Program is a worldclass sales training program, where you have the opportunity to go through sales school, where you learn the best sales methodology and use them in practice for 6 months before going into the field. Sales school is supplemented by communication workshops including standanddeliver and group presentations, as well as classroom learning on IBM's hardware, software and services offerings. It is a very comprehensive sales and leadership training. The Summit Program prepared me for my current sales role and beyond, into any leadership role I want to pursue in the future.  Not to mention my first year has been a lot of fun, with excellent compensation and worklife balance. It is a culture of giving, networking, support, mentorship, and positivity. I have made some of my best friends working for IBM.
Cons: Heavy travel schedule in sales this is a pro for me, but may be a con for others

Pros: Good worklife balance Great coworkers Decent salary not the best, but not the worse either Great technical community Good place to learn about new technologies
Cons: too many levels of management executives with no reporting strucutre?!? very hard to get any straight answers from upper management if your on an technical incentive plan, you can kiss any incentive payment goodbye IBM will make sure you barely make your base salary... employee motivation is down the drain. Lots of very talented employees are fleeing the company because of the abovementioned reasons.

Pros: It's a place where you can work hard and see the results of your work and be recognized for your efforts.  This year's recognition award was hosted in one of the finest hotels in Punta Cana and IBM made all of there feel extremely special.  I've never had as much support by colleagues willing to help me than at IBM. You are working among the brightest, most innovative people willing to assist you.  IBM is a company that has reinvented itself so many times to not only remain relevant but to maintain it's leadership position over well over 100 years.
Cons: Sometimes the large size of the organization can get in the way of itself.  All the help I've noted in the pros sometimes comes at a price where we have too many hands in things.

Pros: You will have good people to work with and a big brand name for your resume. The work load isn't too heavy.
Cons: Raises and bonuses are non existent and have been for years. If you perform well and you are not in sales or an executive, your bonus may be $800. Also, as of 2019 IBM eliminated out of network health coverage. None of the plans offer it though they still call the plans PPO plans, but read the fine print. You are 100% out of pocket for out of network coverage. But the costs go up every year while the coverage declines. IBM used to allow work from home but in an effort to streamline that option is gone, so you will pay to commute not reimbursed and work in an open plan office with picnic tables as desks and not even a coat closet in some locations. Worse case you end up at a WeWork.

Pros: Smart, helpful, capable peers  Finally creating momentum towards a more focused approach on Hybrid Cloud and AI Machine Learning, mostly  Best chance of career growth for those in their early 20's to late 30's
Cons: Traditional command and control thinking from most senior execs, leaders, and managers.  Brands owners of various product lines own the budgets and set the focus too much on "what's in it for IBM" instead of "what's in it for the client".  'Agile' is still a buzzword and not applied in consistent or meaningful ways the vast majority of the time. Agile is more than a framework Scrum, in particular.  Too much downsizing without seeming regard for the performance of the individuals; large, sweeping Resource Allocations RAs = seemingly getting rid of swaths of employees without trying to identify the performance of individuals affected so that we don't lose our best talent.

Pros: Pros are that:  IBM is really big and worldwide, with people doing almost ever imaginable job in IT  IBM is generally on the cutting edge of technology, and must stay that way to survive  IBM has a ton of educational opportunities to help it's people move into new areas, and  IBM pays pretty well
Cons: Cons are that:  Overtime, including weekends, is often expected and sometimes demanded, and that does not leave much time to live  Travel to a job site, sometimes takes over 10 hours by plane, and can occur like that every week, which cuts into the time to live some more  There are so many offshore personnel, and H1 visas, that work for less, that that is somewhat limiting in terms of competition and opportunities, but this is the way of the world now

Pros: Access to the most incredible minds.  Resources that are built in to the giant machine.  Being a part of something great.  Flexibility in finding lateral move jobs.
Cons: You can get lost in the sauce.  Employee upward growth potential is limited once you get 'up there' at least in marketing.  They've been hiring a lot of external agency experienced resources but they don't know anything about how to be and embrace being an IBMer.  The 'new' blood is taking the life out of the passionate IBMers who would give their left leg for the success of the company.  Instead marketers are being shelved or over looked.   Raises are infinitesimal.

Pros: Collaborative tools are a plus. Everybody knows who I work for and I don't have to explain my who my employer is past three letters, IBM. Vacation days are nice, Sick time policy nice, Healthy lifestyle perks such as steps challenges, logging workouts and monetary rewards for keeping an active lifestyle are nice. HSA plan so far has been a positive.
Cons: Salary increases are the most minimal, seems they can barely keep up with inflation. Bonuses for anyone in IT seem to be non existent, banding and layering has diminished my direct reports so now I'm no longer a manager thanks to changes that occurred after acquisition. Travel and hiring bans have been in effect ever since our acquisition took place, nobody knows what the future holds for our team.

Pros: Adopting innovative methods in making learning experience better. Your Learning, Your Career really helps learn besides other tools specific to skill set. I can select a topic of interest and start my learning journey and track progress. These interactive sessions either help download content or transcripts and once you complete the test assessment process ensures that you understand the content. I really appreciate IBMs effort and not only this there are generic badges that allow entire world make use of the badge program and learn topics like IBM Cloud, Block Chain, AI etc.
Cons: I experienced some issues once I move from one org to another within IBM but technical team was very helpful to resolve issues. In some cases due to some issues one of my course tracking was not updating and team was very helpful and since we automated lot of this to adopt AI driven approach in learning experience that may be the issue.

Pros: IBM hires great people  positive, hardworking and bright so the people, and teams are great IBM supports and even promotes telecommuting or working from home which allows for work/life balance IBM offers lots of training and education and a chance to move to many areas of the business IBM hires good management who have good peoplemanagement skills IBM trusts its employees and has good policies in place between management and staff IBM values are excellent
Cons: The company has changed over the years.  It used to reward its employees with trips, motivational awards, company outings etc. This has all but stopped completely.   Quotas were challenging but attainable, allowing one to earn a really good income. That has all but stopped and the environment as of late has been driving employees to meet unrealistic quotas.  Lots of pressure on employees.  Junior employees are micromanaged with all actions tracked.  Topperforming senior sales people are not adequately paid.  Job satisfaction has dropped among my colleagues.  The famous IBM culture is not the same as before, sadly.

Pros: IBM is a recognized name in the IT industry. When people hear it they listen. Everybody still trying to be IBM from old. It just that the old ways have gone out the window. You will have to climb the ladder quickly and bleed big blue. Big blue is your new family now. It is good paying job for management in America, but most other employees are contractors.
Cons: The company outsource to other countries to protect their earnings. I am not bad mouth other countries but when the bottom line means cutting American jobs to save a buck. They should really think how they are hurt America instead of profit. Which they claim they never make all year then at the end seem to pull out for the shareholders.

Pros: Easy on boarding with being able to do everything from signing documents to providing your own photo for your badge.  Great training system with admin mentoring new hire. Decent office. Some benefits are good such as medical. Just starting to implement a one day work from home.
Cons: Below average pay for the high level expectations.   Many restrictions that make it somewhat challenging work environment.   Still using Lotus Notes  but the last I heard they might be implementing Outlook.

Pros: free elearning, opportunity in other career paths, flexible work schedule, 401K
Cons: Lack of job security, disconnect in communications as manager and employees are scattered, hard to focus when no clear objectives defined outside of contract obligations. The raise structure, iwhich is a cost savings for IBM, and does reflect the needs of it employees, it is based on market data from all of North America. It leaves it open for them to always point to an area of the country that is doing poorly and use that as excuse to why they are unable to pay you more money.

Pros: Working at IBM did give me the opportunity to learn a myriad of skills, including professionalism, teamwork, and programming.  I earned a nice salary for the duties I performed.
Cons: Unfortunately, IBM wants you to give every ounce of yourself to your work and the company...and then pays off the United States worker by laying them off right before they reach retirement.  They preach quality, productivity, and efficiency...but will brush those qualities aside for the ability to hire 3rd world country employees at ridiculously low wages...who then must muddle through for years trying to support business and application processes.  IBM Senior Management does not seem to understand that they have destroyed loyalty, ownership, and pride in the company and it's employees by accepting big bonuses on the backs of the United States workers who built the company and  on the United States consumer and tax payer who by their products.

Pros: IBM does an excellent job of laying out the corporate roadmap.  I understand our vision, priorities and how my role fits into the bigger picture to meet these objectives.  I have an amazing manager that trusts me and I am able to execute the best way I see fit.  Having the right manager at IBM makes a big difference! Also, must of the US based employees have the option of working from home.  That is a huge perk for me! I have the discipline to work from home.  I probably work longer house because of it but I really like the flexibility it provides.  I also work with some AMAZING people.  Like in every company there are good and bad but overall most people at IBM are top notch.
Cons: IBM is a big company and continuing to grow.  It's sometimes difficult to find the right person to assist on an engagement.  Also, there are inconsistencies across brands.

Pros: Management was great most of the time. We got 10 vacation and 6 sick days per year + 8 holidays. They matched compensation of my previous employer. They have a a lot of online classes you can take for free. you can work OT on projects if you want.
Cons: Supplemental employees didn't get raises, even after 4 years. No 401K match for Supplementals, so you really need to negotiate your salary up front because the bonuses they offer are only for the first 6 months. Even if you get promoted, you might not get a raise. Health insurance for Supplemental employees was horrible. The worst I have ever seen. Extremely high deductibles and out of pocket maximumsthe amount you have to pay before everything is 100% covered.

Pros: Lot of big empty offices. Getting to work with great people who revolutionised computer science  Many people end up getting paid for noting.
Cons: Its like hug aircraft carrier almost out of supplies , sailing to somewhere it thinks is land. Captain is making decisions based on the gauges and dials which are broken and only really smart engineers know what needs to be fixed. But they are never being asked so they are taking out the lifeboats and leaving the ship.

Pros: I love that I get to work with some of the smartest people in their respective industry. I work on a great small team that allows me to be creative and do things on my own. There are tons of opportunities to shadow people, take on stretch assignments and learn about other parts of the business without having to leave... it's very easy to make a big career change and most of the time it's encouraged. Compensation in my field is unmatched anywhere else. Also, the flexibility to work from home is a plus.
Cons: It's very difficult to get groups to follow cultural changes. A lot of IBMers have been around for a long time, and to get them to change the way we do things is like moving a glacier. I will say that there are great efforts IBM is trying to change, but it really is impossible to make any sort of change until upper management steps in... and even that takes a long while.

Pros: Ability to work from home, travel perks, network with many people and external clients.
Cons: Very poor management  no one knows what you are doing. Typical "CbDers" were lucky to speak with their managers twice a year, of whom were managing 100+ individuals. Your performance is measured entirely on what you say you did at the end of the year.   To be blunt, the company was dishonest about what the CbD program is. The program marketed itself as "strategy & transformation" roles. In reality, the only projects myself or other CbDer's found themselves on were IT implementation projects, which offered little challenge.  IBM's recent marketing campaigns claim the company is involved in analytics, mobile, cloud and social media work. I saw nor heard of any real projects in these fields. These appear to be areas IBM would like to be involved in, but hasn't yet been able to figure out how to do so. It's easy to see right through their fancy marketing after working for IBM.

Pros: If you are looking for a lifetime career you can very well find it IBM. Benefits are good, pay is fair.  It is the rare individual who will "kill it" from a salary standpoint, unless you time it right in sales, or are a GBS Partner.  If you enjoy process overkill with minimal oversight and direction, freedom to shape your role and the opportunity to be involved in a massive team matrix style of management, IBM is an interesting place.
Cons: Surprising the number of "lifers" that are employed/in hiding at this company, many without any experience outside of IBM.  IBM may pride itself on the number of acquisitions and the numbers of "new" IBMrs in the ranks, but those folks quickly figure out the stifling environment and bloated layers of management within the company and realize if they want to do anything innovative they seek roles elsewhere.

Pros: Being out at work as lesbian enabled me to experience helping launch an internal startup  a business development team dedicated to the LGBT+ B2B market. My management also supported my 6month assignment in India with my wife, accompanying me, even though homosexual activity is illegal in India; it said that it couldn't get me out of jail if I were jailed due to the country's laws, but that Pat & I could be fully out as a couple within IBM's four walls; we were and local management and colleagues all were lovely to and inclusive of us. My U.S. management also sponsored my Master's at Columbia while I worked fulltime. All this while being able to mentor and be mentored by amazing LGBT+ colleagues and allies!
Cons: Join an investment bank, rather than IBM, if you want to be wildly wealthy, but you can earn a healthy living here.

Pros: flexibility, Open culture and work/life balance
Cons: It is hard to find good first line and second line managers. Though i do not have much experience dealing with executives, I dont think too highly of them

Pros: While I can't recommend IBM as a place to end a career, it is a good place to be able to make enough to pay the bills while learning Java and all of its associated technologies.  One thing about IBM is that they won't fire you on your first, or even second outings working with their clients, as long as you are trying.
Cons: The old adage about IBM's "culture" is true, and is a hard thing to put up with, but I tolerate it well enough by telling myself that I am traveling in disguise.  Other than that, and the ~standard corporate tricks they attempt to pull on us, it is an ok place to work.  And East Lansing, if you like Michigan at all, is very nice.

Pros: IBM offers self starters opportunities to grow with new roles, new leaders, and education. IBM is a large organization which requires you to network internally with peers, mentors and leaders in many different organizations. You create and build your own reputation. For many roles you can work your own hours but expect it to be 50 hour work weeks at a minumum.
Cons: Don't expect anything to come easy. You need to work with the uncertainty of losing your job, long/unpredictable hours.

Pros: IBM does have some pros. The sheer size and history are incredible. A lot of diversity, and a lot of insanely smart people
Cons: The cons list is too long to be listed cleanly so I'll try to summarize: IBM still uses layoffs in a way that to me is antiquated. A lot of long term people's only skill is surviving at IBM. Expenses and audits are extremely painful. People work in fear of getting a resource action or an audit. Extremely talented people get resourced just because the machine is too big to really notice them.

Pros: Most employees are given the opportunity to work at home. Work hours are generally flexible which helps with life interruptions. The company name looks good on your resume.
Cons: Salary stays flat regardless of performance, promotions, or responsibilities. Almost impossible to get paid training. Benefits cost more each year so with no raises you actually take home less money. The company has one goal only and that is earnings per share target.

Pros: Still a great name on your resume for now  Ability to easily move to new roles based on career aspirations  Great, smart people to work with  Good work/life balance depending on the business unit you work in NOT GBS
Cons: There are many  here are a few:  Moral is low because employees don't feel they are valued  Promotions / raises very scarce unless you are at the lowest or highest levels  Continual reorganizations  chasing changes in the market  Continual territory changes for sales teams  Revenue has not increased in years  profit is obtained and EPS is increased by cutting costs and buying back stock   Costs are cut via selling off parts of the business, constant layoffs called RAs for Resource Action and outsourcing jobs to growth market areas  CEO and SVP team given raises, bonuses, & stock options even though they failed to achieve all stated objectives

Pros: Home office Remote work allowed, decent 401k program, with the right manager advancement is possible
Cons: 1. Required to work from home office, but must pay for all equipment and supplies myself, no reimbursement 2. Lack of Raises  have not had a pay raise in 6 years 3. PBC rating system the pits you against your team mates for the quota allowance of top ratings. last year avg 68 hrs per wk, brought in $450k of addon business I am not a sales person and received praising letters from all customers, I was rated a 2 because there was only 1 2+ available 4. I have worked for 18 years and every year I see more of our very knowledgeable, top performers, in my opinion, either leave or get a Resource Action layed off due to "cost savings" measures

Pros: You can work from home. Get up at 6 am and shut down the laptop after 6 pm. You will have some flexible hours during the day.
Cons: There is no raise. No bonus except for the top 1% contributor. The bonus amount is in the embarrassing scale. The average base salary is consistently below the local market. This is their business model. Believe it or not, they are proud of it. The competent workers left for the fair market value. A lot of employees who are still with the company are either too old to change, or reduce the working hours voluntarily to match the pay, or just too outdated technically to compete in the market to find another job. This is the reality in US. In Indian, the turnover rate is very high since they give minimum pay for the new graduates. Within 23 years, they left for other companies for 100% increase in the salary. No wonder this titanic ship is sinking. Do not jump on it unless you are fresh out of college."

Pros: You will have the opportunity to work with some very smart people that want to make a solid contribution. The professional nonmanagement class does the best they can day in and day out despite a ridiculous amount of administrative red tape
Cons: Every year IBM takes something away in terms of benefits, work life balance, financial incentives, basic common courtesy, respect for employees, and basic integrity. In addition to traveling 1020 hrs and billing 44 hours per week to clients, the latest trend is that you must spend many more hours on IBM's internal social media, more hours on training, mentoring, administrative work, and IBM internal conference calls. An 80 hour work week, week after week,  month after month, year after year is physically and mentally difficult to sustain  and have any kind of fulfilling family life.

Pros: Opportunity abound for those who want it. Conservative workplace, highly virtual where teams are global almost every meeting, extremely high matrixed organization provides challenges for those who want to navigate the system. The workplace is reflective of any megacap company except IBM sets the standard for those companies in business process, use of technology for employees, and work/life balance. Don't get me wrong, get ready to work 50 hours normal week and up to 70 a few weeks in the year when busy. But the work is terribly rewarding. It's great to be an IBMer.
Cons: Large, really large company. Systems galore. Meetings are on the phone almost all the time except when meeting with clients or being assigned to client sites. When you have 420,000 employees, you need that. But, if you don't like having a serial number and being part of the machinery, you may want to rethink IBM.

Pros: Flexible environment for working parents, work from home, etc Salary levels above average in the industry for similar roles Entrepreneurial  room to try and execute your ideas Local level managers and leaders very supportive, positive Loyal customer base and fun innovative solutions Very smart people, helpful teams, overall want to see each other succeed Really care about customers' outcomes Great opportunities for learning and skill building
Cons: Huge percent of time each week preparing updates and reports for your management to pass on to their management Bare bones product management resources to support customers and product enhancements New CEO brought in his politics, polarizing if you don't agree Promotion process unfair and ambiguous, driving great resources out Poor vaccination policy handling 10 week exemption turnaround time, intrusive interviewing , limited 90 day approval, punitive communications

Pros: I can telecommute, that's the only reason I am staying
Cons: Completely lost with objectives, no clarity, a lot of noise

Pros: My resume looks better now, with four years experience at IBM. It helped me get my current job. I was actually introduced to the executive vice president of marketing by my manager with the words... She comes to us from IBM. He seemed impressed.
Cons: There are way too many layers of management at IBM, and they are too far removed geographically from where the vast number of employees are located. I worked in the largest single location where IBM employees are situated... at its heyday, there were upwards of 15,000 employees working there. But many managers aren't located there. My first line of management was several states and at least 1000 miles away. And he managed people in several states. IBM wouldn't even let him travel to meet his people in person.

Pros: Great benefits health, dental, special needs support, etc. Great coworkers for the most part   there have been a few bad apples Flexible work schedule project dependent
Cons: A lot of overhead administrivia both weekly and yearly Disappointing bonus structure Yearly merit increases are a joke Management/organizational structure fluctuates too frequently

Pros: There are no longer any 'Pros' to working at IBM. The company continues to loose customers and market share, the endless cycle of budget cuts, layoffs and increased expectations as eroded the last shreds of decency from the company. People are looking to either get out or protect themselves from the next layoff and seasoned professionals are being let go and replaced with young inexperienced people at 1/2 the salary.
Cons: To many to list. The pressure is unrelenting, no one in marketing does any actual marketing they simply take numbers and information, drop them into powerpoint decks or incredibly myopic 'funnel charts' and 'spin the numbers'. Good, decent, seasoned professionals that have spend years trying to right the ship are being let go and replaced by inexperienced college grads and yet management wants to know why the numbers are off, why the pipeline isn't healthier. Marketing is told to sell and promote solutions that do not actually exist and if they do, don't work. The company is all about 'cloud solutions' but the cloud solutions suffer from poor architecture and constant outages.

Pros: Never ending training available as long as you seek it.   No matter what, IBM has a great reputation with large companies and some SMB.   Great benefit package medical, vacation, personal days, flexibility
Cons: Company is huge therefore the visibility of your business unit is limited to the ivory tower in NY.   If you are talented and make your numbers, your manager will most likely not let you move however if you do not perform the same scenario applies. It's very hard to move.   IBM lacks a CRM software and the entire business runs on an excel sheet.   The administrative tasks take up too much of your time.   Highly layered management. Sometimes makes you wonder what certain roles are for.

Pros: Lots of internal learning.  You can find experts in any relevant field, most of which are happy to talk to you.  Partnership with Apple is huge, brings a lot of publicity.
Cons: Culture.  Too concerned with cost cutting and the bottom line.  Do not treat employees very well, minimal perks.  In consulting, they staff you where they need you, not based on interests.  You can get stuck on a project in one role for years without much growth.  They give their entry level consultants work that could be done by interns.

Pros: During one of the most exciting times of the intersection between business and technology in history, IBM is leading the way to reinvent itself and create an environment of partnerships and countless opportunities. IBM gives a platform for employees to build a customercentric P&L to drive growth for product and service lines and the company while delivering for customers.
Cons: Like any large enterprise, the larger the program responsibilities the bigger are the challenges. Although opportunities are in front of us, the internal silo's get in the way of the obvious. Employees who embraces challenges and seek opportunities through focus and resilience to build internal and external partnerhips, will thrive. Those who are a mere employees hoping to be guided, might not. You can look at it as a pro or con, your choice.

Pros: IBM is a great place to work, if you are a minority or a woman.  If you're a woman and show the slightest spark of competence, you will fly past your male counterparts, whether or not you deserve it.  Because of this, there are so many horrendous first and second level managers, as well as Senior and STSM level technical leaders.
Cons: The only way to get into the top ranks is to be the toady of a midlevel manager.  If you are really unfortunate, you will work for an EO candidate who will surely take credit for your accomplishments.  If you are really lucky, you'll work for one of the dwindling number of career managers 30+ years with the company who will be straight with you.

Pros: Amazingly smart people! If you have a chance to work with IBM Research  take it ! Fantastic organization. IBM'ers are wicked smart and very professional.  IBM really gets behind clients if they are hired. Great job experience for Band 7, 8 and 9's  younger less experienced resources but plan an exit strategy.
Cons: 1. IBM is very hard to do business with as far as clients are concerned  from a contracting perspective as they expect everyone to bend to their Ts&Cs, 2. Sales teams are cutthroat and will run you over for deal credit  make sure if you get involved in a "deal" that you have in writing what our "cut" is up front   sometimes even that won't matter and 3 make your sales target EVERY YEAR or you will be fired immediately. No "performance improvement  plan"  just good bye and so long.

Pros: Most of the people I met at IBM were nice for the most part. I was able to work from home %100 of the time, which was great.
Cons: IBM is in continuous layoff mode. And, they will never stop. IBM has no loyalty to their employees, nor to any of their clients. I was on a profitable account, and they still laid off a ton of people, leaving the client with no one to fulfill their needs. IBM expects you to work most weekends or "volunteer" but you can't claim vacation, sick time, nor holiday on the weekend. Way too much paperwork and old processes that take a lot of time away from actual work. I moved from the previous contract company on the same account. As soon as we went from CSC to IBM, our paperwork increased 10 times.

Pros: Big company presents lots of opportunities.  Most of the people I worked with were bright and good to work with.  It's such a big company that there are lots of different areas to work in, and I believe moving around is not too hard if you're qualified.
Cons: Being a small cog in a big machine  ocassional bureaucratic headaches.  The pay was adequate, but perhaps felt a bit on the low end vs. competitors.  Benefits felt a little stingy.  It was a bit disapointing when I was there that a big portion of bonuses were tied to the division's performance and the overall firm's performance, so in a time when parts of the business I had nothing to do with were under performing, my compensation was was lower.

Pros: Constantly reinventing itself in a fast moving industry You have great latitude for being entrepreneur and lead Great focus on driving innovative offerings in the market place and help our customers to transform themselves and disrupt in the marketplace Ability to move up and laterally in broad solution areas Right business strategy: focus on high value areas, focusing on delivering outcome vs products Great investment in employee skills and industry knowledge Ability to work remotely for the most part Strong values and customeroriented culture
Cons: Takes a bit of effort to understand the organization and the broad portfolio Can take a while to adjust to a remote way of working.  Most internal meetings are over conference calls, which has positives but could take a bit of effort to adjust and get used to Technology companies work in fast moving environments to specific divisions can change direction relatively quickly.  People who can't easily adjust/adopt change might find it difficult.

Pros: I personally enjoy who I work with and how understanding my coworkers and managers are.  For example when I give input or suggestions in team meetings I feel that what I say is valued and taken to heart.
Cons: I feel that the apprenticeship program has still has quite a bit of a ways to go. However, I am thankful I was chosen to be part of it. With that said, I think IBM needs to think about having more training "handson" and less video watching. Rather, try to have apprentices shadow people more often and see the role they are training to do. Videos can only help so much before the brain turns to mush. Changing things up helps the mind stay active.

Pros: High, competitive salary. Could not believe I was making X amount out of college.  Access to the best training whether that be online on in person free!  Great health insurance  Good reputation . . . Everyone always looks very impressed when they find out that I work for IBM
Cons: Ambiguity within the first year of job. Had no idea what I was doing for about 10 months  Front line manager isn't helpful or open for questions please note, this was with MY manager. There are about 10 others that I hear are really helpful and great leaders... I just got unlucky

Pros: IBM still does have a decent benefits package  Insurance, sick leave.  Even though the cost is much higher that we have paid in the past, it is still much lower and coverage is better than what you can get on the outside.
Cons: Hours  management thinks that we should be living, dying breathing IBM.    We are penalized for things that are out of our control.  Lack of respect from management.  Many feel that we do not have the intelligence to do our jobs.

Pros: IBM has always been very respectful of worklife balance and time off for life events, etc. Leaders are generally very accessible and willing to engage all employee levels. The work can be very rewarding.
Cons: The spreadsheet mentality means that they may not always completely understand how to value a good employee whose benefit to the company rises above their bottom line or utilization tallies particularly in the area of User Experience and other creative/design roles. It was NOT always like this here. It seems back in the earlier part of the decade, we were encouraged to "Do the Right Thing" and were rewarded for our efforts and risk in a more organic way.

Pros: Good technical environment semiconductor business to expand knowledge base.  Empowered to do experiments as needed, to find answers to ongoing problems.
Cons: Penny pinching.  CEO and executives are focused ONLY on "EPS" Earnings Per Share, and the price of common stock.  After all, this how they grow their personal wealth...through stock options.  Living in constant fear of being sold off or outsourced.  No conferences allowed.  Very little new equipment purchased for our lab.  Seem to be "cooking the books", for years now, to make the division more attractive to potential suitors. Forget about meaningful salary increases.  Many, many years since I saw one of those.

Pros: Work from home though IBM seems to be reducing this option for some positions  Good, dedicated coworkers at the lower levels
Cons: Lack of raises  Lots of talk about customer focus but focus is on $$$ even when it results in significant negative impact to customers  Training provided is only online and primarily sales focused  Repeated layoffs in the U.S.  IBM execs think of employees only as a cost that they want to eliminate.  Everyone is always waiting for the call regardless of performance ratings.  Total lack of respect for employees

Pros: Working at home.  Make 95K sitting home, eating chips, and checking your email every 2 hours.  Another good reason is that IBM looks good on your resume.  Finally, you get really good at dealing with politics and difficult angry people who are this way because they are stressed from being overworked and forced to achieve unrealistic goals.
Cons: Hard to advance career even when you really try hard  and  LOTS of red tape to go through to get anything done.  I always tell people working at IBM is 90% filling out forms / 10% doing actual technical work.  IBM needs to start caring about employees again and we will care about the company.  Until then, we will be unproductive.

Pros: Company offers wide variety of opportunities for different roles, career paths  IF you can get support of your manager.
Cons: Very few opportunities to build interpersonal and team relationships with colleagues and coworkers as most are work from home. Spend lots of time on conference calls with cast of dozens or more. Very slow movement on projects due to "too many cooks," political wrangling and landscape. Difficult to build trust, as many are individual contributors focus on impressing management and rather than focusing on projects that help move the organization forward.

Pros: Smart colleagues, wellrespected company that's a household name, work on challenging and important initiatives, most decisions based on facts and the merits of the argument.
Cons: Bureaucratic and complex. Company does not invest in its employees as much as it used to, pays the minimum to retain employees. You need to be good at setting boundaries because there are major work/life balance issues with expectations that you be connected 24x7. Lack of promotions unless you are politically connected. Feeling of social isolation due to overreliance on technology and conference calls rather than face to face meetings.

Pros: Excellent benfits for employees paired with a generally relaxed environment and very good work/life balance.
Cons: All levels of management like to spout corporate BS about people being assets and looking forward while entire focus is on how much money they can post to Wall St this quarter. This causes many internal tools to fail to work properly as resources are pulled of projects to work on others or just laid off resulting in less efficient working conditions. They are now asking how to keep contractors furloughed to below 40/hrs per week without paying any extra. Raises are still on hold for at least this year, maybe next for contratcors and employees.

Pros: Free parking and being in low traffic location.
Cons: Besides the low pay, this offshore "answer" ends up being the mojo contributing to a culture that exemplifies the many absurdities that might be found in a Dilbert cartoon i.e  on demand seating policy at this facility for instance.  It's Beige Man, in not only the physical surroundings, but in the energy, the vibe, the leadership/management of people.  Creative, Innovative, and statusquo challengers will find it stifling and consistent with the same ole' lumbering bureaucracy where people are just numbers to be manipulated.

Pros: Opportunity to gain true global experience and to meet IT people from many other companies who have been outsourced by IBM.  Opportunity to work with many other large companies and gain the insight of how they run.
Cons: "Resource Actions"/layoffs all the time, never know when your number is up, exempt employees are often expected to work 60 to 80 hours a week and often form months at a time.  Often the job requires travel, still need to do all the work with what hours remain in the week.  Compensation is not that of the competition unless you are a new hire and negotiate real well.  This year the lady running IBM canceled variable pay.

Pros: One of the most enjoyable work environments if you consider fellow employees and cultural diversity. Some of the best engineers and other performers worked their way through the big machine and mostly moved on if they were able to. Solid "B" performers can make a decent, somewhat remunerative career. There are still opportunities and challenges every day.
Cons: Hierarchical, paternalistic, minimal financial incentives. Asinine predetermined evaluation process, which is designed to minimize payroll expense, rather than improve performance.  A mixture of gameplayers and very hard workers managed to maintain course, innovating for a company that only seeks shareholder value at any cost. They've long ago lost the "carrotandstick" approach; taken away all the carrots; it's all stick.

Pros: Absolutely amazing company to work for. The possibilities are truly limitless. The network of support you get just by becoming an IBMer is truly unmatched. Excellent benefits and possibilities of commissions.
Cons: Metrics DDRs are judged on aren’t 100% determined on how hard the rep works. The OTE of $35k/yr. is impossible to calculate ahead of time. It is supposed to be if you get 100% of your quotas then you’ll get the $35k. However, there are reps not getting any of that $35k and reps getting way more. Also it can be very defeating making cold calls/emails with no response, hence not making numbers, and not getting any commission contrary to working hard.

Pros: my teammates who are typically smart and hardworking and frequently considered to be industry experts.  Option to work out of home office was nice.
Cons: Miserable morale and loss of respect for employees.  Shifting people out of the business when their skills and knowledge of how to get things done will be lost forever.  Recent restructuring created many new senior exec jobs just before the Resource Action which eliminated many lower level employees.  Employee's were given low performance ratings to ensure they do not get their bonus on the way out the door, however, senior execs will all get bonuses this year.

Pros: Vast, raw, untapped opportunities abound for your needs for exposure, selfsatisfaction, personal validation, professional breadth and depth of expertise and experiences, and conditioning to not only boringold direct reporting relationships, but REAL and topquality matrix reporting relationships. You can be happy here in 3 ways: personally, professionally and organizationally, and you can do this if you approach IBM as a place where you best contribution is made by figuring out how to squeeze the most of it.
Cons: Do not come here if you think you're going to be led in to everything you need. Do not come here if you have no idea what you need. Seriously, I'm not kidding, GO TO THERAPY before or shortly after coming to IBM to understand what are your personal needslike REALLY your personal needs: are you an introvert, an extrovert, a gogetter, a centrist, a selfdeceiver, a selfvalidator, needy, selfaggrandizing, narcissistic, unsure of yourself, oversure of yourself, etc. etc...only come here if you know what you need. If you don't know, don't come here. Second, don't come here if you don't understand what you could possibly build on your resume in the 1st 100 days. I firmly believe that 1 year at IBM is worth 24 years anywhere else. If you can't put 23 things on your resume in 100 days or less working for IBM, then go back to therapy and see my first point. Lastly, there is no organization to be FOUND at IBM...none. It's flat, with no more than 11%14% of its employees as people managers. IBM's organization lives IN YOUR HEADso get it all up in your head and figure it out. If you are the type of person who needs a very clear organization structure and you freak out without clarity, then please don't come here.

Pros: Good entrylevel opportunity  Infinite wealth of knowledge available to absorb  Very flexible hours
Cons: Extremely difficult to move up or leave a department you can be a victim of your own success and as a result, doors can be closed for you  Hostile review process promotes cutthroat environment with peers If everyone in your team cures a different type of cancer individually, one of you will still get fired for underperforming in comparison with your peers  TOO MANY PROCESSES sometimes you need to create a process to follow a process that has been created to conform to a different process  Too many levels of management. Upper level management never knows what's going on.  Some divisions of IBM are so badly managed that the turnover rate is over 60% GTS for example  NEVER WORK AT A GDF

Pros: You will work with incredibly smart people in IBM. You'll work on really interesting projects. You'll have the ability to change jobs and learn many different parts of the business. IBM is shaping itself to remake enterprise IT for the cloud, harness the power of analytics and big data, and drive applications to follow a systems of engagement paradigm.
Cons: It's a very tough climate internally right now. Constricting budgets, resource actions, minimal raises and benefits eroding slowly over time. Most people want to be at IBM longterm and are holding on for dear life as senior management try to steer the ship to more profitable waters.

Pros: IBM acquired the company I worked for a few years ago.  Surprisingly, the transition into the IBM world was relatively painless, at least for me.  IBM has decent benefits and a good 401k plan.  Many employees work from home, which is a great advantage, saving on commuting time, gas and wear and tear on your car.
Cons: Senior management makes most decisions in a vacuum without regard for the effect it will have on employees and our customers.  Middle management is mediocre at best, with a few shinning stars. There does not seem to be an opportunity to move into other jobs although it's touted that IBM has a career path for employees.

Pros: Well paying career, even for entry level positions  Work from home for many consulting positions  Travel is well compensated and if you can put up with it, you get to experience a lot
Cons: Managerial staff does not pay attention/care about your success at all  To excel, you need experience, but most people are interested in only their development and refuse to help you get said experience  Regarding the last point, hours can be insane, including required weekends. If you travel, say goodbye to a social life, and be sure your relationships can take extreme stress.

Pros: There are mant opportunities to work on large, complex environments the kind if experience it can be difficult to get unless you work for a large software firm. In spite of everything management can do,  there are still some amazing minds at IBM, and many wonderful technicians who are dedicated to their customers success.
Cons: 1 The culture is one if extreme distrust, due in large part to promotion of glad handers and yesmen.  People who actually work hard and are willing to speak truth to power are all too frequently marked for the many layoffs. 2 Far too top heavy. 3 Management far too distracted by industry fads at the expense of customers, employees and the long term health of the business.

Pros: Coworkers and first level and midlevel managers were some of the best and brightest I've worked with. Good teamwork.   Base salary was very good.  Flexible schedules and work from home are commonplace.
Cons: A couple times each year there will be a resource action with layoffs ranging from less than a hundred to multiple thousands. Morale suffers.   Most of my coworkers joined IBM through an acquisition. In other words, most did not choose IBM and apply for an opening there.   IBM delays matching your 401k contributions until Dec. 15, at which time IBM makes a onceayear contribution for the previous twelve months of accrued match. If you leave IBM or IBM lays you off before the company match contribution is made, too bad; you receive $zero match for the entire year; no prorated match.  There are so many silos and divisions that there are duplicate processes.   IBM uses Notes for email and calendar.

Pros: I worked at the Almaden research center and in the Yorktown research center Great research with stateoftheart equipment. Very knowledgeable people, who are also friendly and reliable Still good core values of the IBM company, with people doing their whole 40year career at IBM Personnel encouraged to patent, publish and go to conferences Internal recognition through awards
Cons: Compensation below microelectronics industry average  Hard to obtain information on the technology orientation for future processor generations Company starts to rely too heavily on process improvement rather than disruptive innovation Excessive bureaucracy Recurrent budget restrictions even though IBM Research is highly profitable

Pros: IBM makes a difference in people's lives by applying innovation and technology to create the future. IBM is unique in that it is the only technology company to reinvent itself through multiple technology eras and economic cycles. In 20+ years at the company I have continually found new career opportunities. I have stayed most of all because of the smart, ambitious and talented IBMers I have worked with over the years.
Cons: Given its size and reach IBM can be slow moving. It can be difficult to see one's individual mission as essential to the whole. In a time of industry disruption, the pressure to keep skills relevant is relentless. As IBM moves our clients to the future, we as IBMers must constantly move ourselves to the future as well.

Pros: Good variety of projects and locations. Personnel are friendly and professional. Excellent opportunity to work with technical experts. Flexible schedule and remote opportunities are a big plus.
Cons: For a supposed leader in tech, far too many inefficient processes. Receiving a badge and a login for key systems took way too long after completing a background check and coming on site. Processes for protocols were not transparent and required asking multiple people. The need to call tech support to change a password is incomprehensible and inexcusable.

Pros: Good coworkers, decent pay, good schedule.
Cons: TERRIBLE upper management, AWFUL corporate vision, constant lay off, furloughs, and pay cuts.
