 Opportunities for internal movement
Cons:
Leadership tolerates drama, lying, backstabbing
 Lack of accountability for managers and individual contributors
 Star players are often invisible to management, even their own managers
 Old fashioned office politics are strongly encouraged and required above a certain level
 It's often the most destructive employees who get the most positive attention squeaky wheel gets applauded when they fix things they broke?
 Very short term memory of causeandeffect consequences same mistakes made repeatedly by leadership
 Selfcentered culture, cliquish, judgmental and eager to exclude from the "in" groups
 Very much a sinkorswim organization, but talent is valued less than "playing the politics game"
 The organization will consume your life if you let it, some managers don't accept that you have a life outside of work
 Manager's word always taken as solid gold by leadership
 Overall very toxic environment

Pros: Great benefits, resources, and the network. One of the best place to intern or do a 6month coop as an engineer.
Cons:
Large corporation. Easy to get lost in the crowd of people with similar skills. Bad communication amongst different department and business units.

I was hired as a Hardware Engineer intern for the "Cisco Choice Program." The uniqueness of the program is that if you do well during your internship you will get hired back and get to interview the managers of different business units within Cisco and pick which Business Unit you want to work for.

Due to the bad economy and higher ups decisions, they decided to cut all hardware engineers position for the Cisco choice program leaving only Software and MBA students.

Pros:
A great opprtunity to work with some serioulsy talented people, especially out in the regions
  Benefits and salary are above the industry norm
  Ability to expand your experience through different roles within the company, out in the regions and at HQ
Cons:
You have to wonder how some people especially at corporate are still  in their roles.. they should have gone a long while ago,  while some of the hard working, talented individuals have either moved on, or will soon do so, due to high frustration levels.
  Still an old boys club mentality at the top...
  Many executives have been there too long... need to bring in some fresh blood and a new way of thinking.
  Recently lost its way with too much restructuring... it is breeding discontentment and bad morale in a big way.

Pros: Candid and transparent management, great sense of community and drive to support employees worklife balance.  Truly a good company that does good to the world,  evidenced by actions, executive focus and dollars invested.
Cons: Very slow in making all sorts of decisions. Most functions perform their work with outdated or homegrown tools and systems which hinder productivity.  Moving up the organisation requires honed social ability and a strong established network, more so than good work and performance. Does not offer competitive pay,  and becoming too complacent on being rated #1 Place to work to keep workforce.  External candidates will be paid considerably higher than those already employed, as the market has leapfrogged a clearly broken internal salary range system, and a growing backlog of salary increases and promotions.

Pros: Since working for Cisco after graduating my growth has been tremendous. Cisco is a place where there are many experts you can learn from and gain experience especially if you're like me, someone out of school two years.
Cons:
Promotions are slow and its difficult to get recognition. I am lucky in that my manager and I have a good working dialogue and I know he is listening to my concerns. 

If you're ambitious and damn good at your job, you'll start to feel frustrated often at Cisco. Reason being promotions are slow and those who are the lowest performers are rewarded by keeping their job and those who are worth their salt aren't promoted fast enough. Of course, I'm sure this is common with large companies. 

In my opinion, Cisco needs to recognize fresh talent quickly, give them me opportunities to grow and responsibilities, and promote them quickly.

Pros: They pay well, especially for employees who live outside of Silicon Valley and have a lower cost of living. They encourage remote working, so you have a lot of flexibility. Wellknown and respected in IT circles. Benefits are generous. Many people work there for 20+ years.
Cons: The culture is very corporate, full of things that seem straight out of Dilbert. Jargon, corporate politics, SLOW pace and red tape much of the time. If you're not an engineer, it's hard to feel appreciated for what you contribute. The layoffs seem haphazard. They say that it helps week out lowperformers, but they give blanket percentages across the organization, so obviously many good employees are caught and it leaves the remaining teams to pick up work for several people. Doing this over and over is demoralizing. Many of my coworkers only stay because they don't think they can find a remote job that will pay as well. Not exactly inspiring.

Pros: Executive leadership team is good, says the right things, sometimes even do the right things. I like that there is a big sense of family when there are personal challenges of employees. The People Deal, and the focus on employees is very good, and highly appreciated.
Cons: A behemoth of a company where collaboration could be optimized so much more, although it is better than it was 10 years ago. Career movements should be much easier for internal candidates than it is, of course there are job movements but should be more supported. Each team has its own employee experience based upon the leader, and of course you can expect this but it is difficult to get around this or through this if you find yourself on a team that doesn't quite gel with you. There are teams that have a fantastic, warm culture, while other teams play favorites, politics and there is no accountability. Lastly, every year we are expected to cut x% from the budget, so it became an uninspiring place to work if you value innovation, large transformation, or you care about the customer experience.

Pros:
What I can only describe as the "Cisco Heartbeat". From the minute you start at Cisco, you start to feel part of something bigger. We are one united global team.  At Cisco we train hard and push each other to drive business success, so we have the privilege of giving that success back. We are on a mission to impact 1 billion lives globally, and I know thats only the beginning.
 Cisco is a world class company, and an industry leader in networking technology.
 As big as Cisco is, they provide each and every employee with the tools and support they need to truly be the best version of themselves.
 Hands down the best office culture I have ever experienced.
 Incredible benefits for all employees
 We have a pingpong table in the office
Cons:
It may seem biased but I have no cons about Cisco...
 The interview process is VERY TOUGH compared to other companies, but it is only to find people who are driven enough to do great things in this world.

Pros: Flexible work culture, Can work from home regularly. Benefits such as 401K and bonus are very good. Can move internally, i had 6 jobs in 11 years.
Cons:
Very complex org going through changes. Lack of transparency on how promotions are given out promotions. Those who get promoted do not get any new responsibilities and in the subsequent annual reviews you get dinged for not performing at a level higher than earlier.
Cannot blame the people managers as people are graded on a curve and managers are forced to follow directions from VP down.

Pros: Cisco Systems hires brightest talents in the market. Welleducated, open minded, experienced, sociable, eager to face new challenges, constantly pushing themselves out of the comfort zone and working on continuous improvement. Great management and very supportive. I did not feel hierarchy pressure and could address my concern or question to the top of the top of senior leadership. Senior leadership always backs salesforce out there in the field, generating demand and making revenue for the company. Cisco Systems also emphasizes internal mentorship and coaching programs, pushes team for trainings and continuous learning. Great company to work for.
Cons: Supply chain, logistics, slow internal processing clock speed leads to issues with customer experience and satisfaction. Sometimes, it is easier to cancel the initial order placement and request a new shipment, which has high chances to arrive early. Sometimes it is hard to engage security team to make a demo or pilot for a customer whose business is small or medium, perhaps this has improved in the last three years.

Pros: Some excellent people, immensely talented, committed and hardworking.  Demanding environment, with continuous challenges.  I've never had a dull day in 13 years working for the company.  There are still opportunities for international assignments, but becoming more challenging than in the past. Compensation and rewards are good, depending on level.
Cons: Company still too corporate focused in spite of its global remit.  There is a need for a massive change management exercise to bring the culture to be more process orientated, and for decisionmaking to be more objective.  Too much change ordered from top down but with ineffective change management below VP and even Director level.

Pros: IMO Cisco is positioned as the number 1 company in the world in IT.  We have innovative products across the spectrum of IT infrastructure  data center, collaboration i.e. phones, webex, business video, networking route/switch and security.  It is a constantly growing, dynamic company with great leadership.  It gives back and does the right thing.  A very high integrity company.  We have great work flexibility and are able to leverage the best collaboration tools in the world to stay connected and aligned with our mission.  We provide strategic solutions that can help solve business challenges of all companies around the world  i.e. speed, agility, flexibility, productivity.
Cons: It's a big company.  With that there is a degree of complexity to the business.  Some of our services business is a bit more difficult, giving our historical "box selling" orientation.  But that is changing a lot.

Pros: Stability its not going anywhere, opportunity to work remotely, and the potential for professional growth.
Cons:
At some level, the emperor has no clothes.  This is from a nonsales, support function perspective.

Compensation model for nonsales personnel was consistently below market, and there was a pollyannish devotion to stock options.  Who remembers "The drive to 35?"  Unwillingness to recognize that it had become a largecap, slowgrowth company, and needed to move from an options to a restricted stock model. 

Managers have too much control over review process, and there is too little emphasis on rewarding talent in a fair and consistent manner.   Perception is much more important than reality  e.g. review process too focussed on peripheral "initiatives," rather than  business results.  

Inconsistent messages   selling the world on telecommuting, but making it difficult for your own employees to do it as well.

Pros: Compensation, benefits are very good.  Performance based equity.  Work time is flexible.  Component vendors will bend over backwards to get their product designed in.  Engineering staff is top notch.   Good people to work with.   HW design tools are best avail.
Cons: HW engineering a dying breed at Cisco.  Focus is on SW feature delivery.  SJ is the center of excellence and the remote US locations are just support sites.  Development teams are global  expect late night conf calls with china, india, malaysia.  Internal support of design tools is weak.  Layoffs have become a way of life.  Morale has dwindled.

Pros: Challenging if in the correct group and, or project. Opportunity exists to learn about global business and current industry trends an challenges impacting long term global expansion and corporate sustainability. There is much groundbreaking initiatives on the radar or in progress and an willingness to do it right. Sense of urgency is present regarding these efforts and within the LOBs associated to the work.
Cons: Bloated. Not everyone is doing their bit. Significant passing the buck, and for every achiever, there are multiple non achievers. A significant degree of complacency, which includes biding time for longer term employees. People are staying for the wrong reasons, sapping energy and motivation of those that care. Too many contractors with core knowledge covering for SME roles. Allows the FTEs/SMEs ability to cruise and internal business knowledge is being diluted.

Pros: Cisco hires solid performers. Most employees seem to have typeA personalities and are very results focused. For a big company, this is a fast paced environment. Compensation is good: bonuses historically have been generous and it's the same for restricted stock grants for more senior employees. Cisco is focused on innovating and leading in their respective areas. Cisco is also good about giving employees the opportunity to move around the company, take on different positions and learn new skill sets. The company also has a very forwardthinking mindset when it comes to working remotely.
Cons: As with any big company, there can be multiple levels of management. This can be frustrating at times. Politics can be an issue in some organizations. Employees also have to set boundaries when it comes to the work/life balance. If you don't set boundaries, you'll likely get burned out.

Pros: Cisco is a fantastic company in terms of benefits  I've never worked for a company that offered more.  Salaries and bonuses are good, but there's much more  all kinds of insurance and healthrelated programs that help both the employee and the community.  Always something interesting going on.  Always a chance to get involved and do new things, both inside and outside of work.
Cons:
It is painfully hard to get things done.  Every department and every project and every process seems to be in flux all the time.  Too many hands in every pot.  Processes are too cumbersome.  Too many meetings, too much confusion.  It's a big, big company, with all the usual bigcompany problems.

Note: this perspective is from a person who joined on as a result of her smaller, privatelyheld company getting acquired by Cisco.

Pros: great company with mart people!  new leadership has big shoes to fill, that said  Mr Robbins knows exactly what he's dealing with and has a strong vision and support front he Board about what Cisco needs to do differently going forward, and lastly, i was the proudest employee when I worked for this company  in touch with the community and the humans that make Cisco strong, and Cisco takes and time and enables good things for its employees and the communities its in.
Cons: its a big company with some big company problems  and yes there are politics and BS that goes on  no different than most places.  in my opinion, its an authentic place with a culture that has allowed people to have a POV and speak up about it without a problem if done productively.  there have been lots of people changes since mr Robbins stepped in as CEO, good newws and some not so much.

Pros: For a 70,000 person, global company, there are so many things to be PROUD of in working for Cisco. As an LGBT leader at Cisco, I am happy to be myself, and encourage others to do the same. There is tremendous executive support for our LGBT brothers and sisters at Cisco, across the globe. Cisco's continued 'foot on the gas pedal' delivering on Inclusion & Diversity aren't just words, rather, actions that continue to grow. #CiscoPRIDE is alive and well.
Cons: The only 'Con' I can muster up is the opportunity to find new opportunities within Cisco for many people. Cisco is not a high growth company, so not adding 100s of jobs/week, like some others. That said, there is tremendous opportunity for cross teaming, working on stretch assignments, and raising your hand to do 'other' things.

Pros:
Great training second to none for early in career
Great for making key contacts in early career development
Corporate culture is very forward looking and emphasises more humanitarian principles than most large corporate companies
Perks are very good, wages paid 75% to the highest average in the field
Cons:
Still a large corporate, as such you'll still encounter people playing the corporate game, even in the early in career programs.
Unfortunately, expect a lot out of you, especially if you are working in the Asia Pacific region. Burnout and overwork is common among colleagues.

Pros: Cisco is stable, a fun place to work, and you can make of it what you will. I have been with the company for 10+ years and it's still a place I usually enjoy going every morning. When I wanted more responsibility, I just did it. In my experience you don't need to ask, just do it. Cisco encourages risktaking, but if you're not a risktaker, you'll do fine. Just do your job well. Free soda, popcorn, 4 wks vacation, generous compensation, and a company that is growing are all reasons Cisco is a great place to work.
Cons: Cisco's history of decentralization makes it hard to get the entire company to move in one direction. It can be hard to get crossfunctional jobs done and it's not uncommon to discover other groups are doing a similar thing as you!

Pros:
Coming from university and straight to this as my first job I couldn't be happier, I work under a recruitment company and situated here at Cisco Systems.  The lifestyle and environment has surpassed my expectations of what the standard should be for a globally recognized company, compared to friends and family work environments and my previous experiences I can without a doubt say I am fortunate enough to be working at this professional establishment.

Everyone here is very friendly, there are lots of community events and it is very employee focused in the sense they put us first and make sure we are happy, not too stressed and make it fun to work here. He has good services too, on site carwash, dry cleaning, large choice of food in the canteen with special weekly dishes and much more. 

I can happily say this is one of the best companies to work at, and I would not leave unless I really had to in order to pursue my career.
Cons: Nothing I can think of.

Job Title: Sales, Channel Sales, Pre-Sales Technical And Business Development
Pros: Having a long tenure at Cisco I enjoyed many roles and worked in multiple theatres. Cisco culture was printed and updated on the badge, but ultimately it was the people Cisco attracted. It meant working with the best of the best and many are still close friends.
Cons: Worklife balance was hard at times, but often this was selfinflicted because Cisco has such a strong culture to do what it takes and not let anybody down. There is always too much to do and so much opportunity to do more, so Cisco requires one to be a master at anticipating and prioritising. You must Network, collaborate and delegate to strike the right balance.

Pros: In some ways, Cisco still operates like a nimble startup constantly reinventing itself. They are quick to adapt new technologies and innovations as long as that is where the market is heading. Change is the only thing that's constant, and they have no qualms to sacrifice long beholden programs or projects  in other words, no sacred cows. All this said, these are what I believe keeps Cisco successful, plus you gotta love their new slogan, "To be the best company in the world, and the best company for the world".
Cons: It is a big company, and you will feel invariably feel the beauracracies largely attributed to big companies. To get promoted you really have to invest considerable amount of time doing all the extra other things. Time that you would normally like to spend with your family. However, if you are satisfied with your current level then the workload is comparable to silicon valley standards.

Pros:
Cisco is an amazing Company!  I always feel empowered to go above and beyond my given role. Here at Cisco you have many opportunities to network and get involved. You can become a Mentor, join an ERO such as Conexion attend amazing conferences such as Women of Impact.
I love that Cisco is a Global Company and I’m able to work across all regions in my day to day role! I feel that Cisco does a great job in creating a Culture of Inclusion.
Cons: For some, Cisco may be a bit intimidating based on the vastness of the Company.  However, once you begin to network and get involved you will quickly realize that it isn’t that intimidating, and people are very willing to connect with you.  Either to share best practices, join a shadow program or perhaps sign up to do a stretch assignment.

Pros:
Great vision from CEO  Chambers turned internet "plumbing" company into software/application/unified communications/collaboration/video/data center & server company in the last 510 years.
Great sales execution
Great product line  It almost sells itself
Good pay & commission checks because of reason above
Ability to work remotely
Empowerment  WebEx conferencing, softclient IP phone allows above
Flexibility  Allows personal choices for work devices such as Macbook Pros at company's expense! & iPhones
Cons:
Slow career advancement
Unclear on how to get promotions
Company is severely cutting costs  no more free beverage, home internet, etc.
Perceived poor leadership from development organization  most of our technology & new product lines are gained through acquisitions
Salary increases are very little  expect none to 35% a year
Pace of work at least in sales is FAST. Must control own work life balance.

Pros:
The flexibility to work from home. 
Worked with some really talented people.
Lots of training/education
Good pay for contractors
Cons: As a contractor  I observed a lot of office politics!  Communications group puts way to many senseless ppt presentations together and redundant forms of communication.  Not even sure if people are listening or awake during large webex meetings  dead silence during Q&A's.  I was never een sure what exec management team actually did. For those that have worked there a long time, which seemed like alot of people, they are stuck in a rut and aren't open to anything new and do it they way it's always been done.  The virtuall office McCarthy Ranch  can't really be utilized by contractors  squatters take over the spaces that are supposed to be open to all.

Pros: Amazing People, Great Products and the juggernaut of the Internet.  Lots to be learned, and 30 years of experience in high tech.
Cons: It's not the company it used to be.  A massive revolving door these days, and a focus on lowercost of doing business.  Growth potential is probably very limited, and more likely, this is a company that will be shrinking a lot over the next 5 to 10 years.

Pros:
The managers over here are constantly trained to maintain balance btween all the employees in a team.
There is no micro management at all.
Your weekdays are yours, your holidays are yours
Best work life balance.
Free AC Gym provided in Bangalore main campus.
Yearly Complete health checkup is done at free of cost.
Company provided 50K before tax as bonus for each employee in india amidst covid crisis.
You can move from one team to another with "internal movement" which will help you get rid of managers  if yu don't like them or the tech stack.
 Of course, you need to stay on the same role for an year untill you move for another one

Identity  where you travel in the world, people will recognize the company name.
Cons:
Salaries are not upto market standards.
 All managers are not the same.
 Some managers won't handle there team's well and it results of employees leaving.
 Food is not for free 🙂
 Onsite travel is not up to that much.

Pros:
You can work in the office or  at home
Most people  care about what they are doing
Quality products
Great Benefits
Looks great on a resume
You get to make a lot of contacts in a short time
Cons:
To many ASR’s in the company who have a sense of entitlement
Mid management often doesn’t get it
Too many politics involved to get promoted
Most ODs are just trying to climb the ladder and don’t  do a good job in leading teams
AMs have gotten lazy and forgotten how to cold call
People who should be fired continue to make lateral moves and are never let go
Cisco needs to clean out the bottom 5% every year and they have gotten away from that practice.
Too many outside consultants
The whole review process  is a joke
Too many internal meetings when you should be out with clients
You have to leave to get promoted to higher spot at times

Pros: Stability  no one is going to buy Cisco any time soon though there is still attrition.  Incredible wealth of resources available.  Lots of supersmart people running around.  Lots of market share in every virtually every product line, and the cachet that comes with the Cisco name.
Cons: Huge company.  Too many competitors with better technology.  Cisco can't be expected to turn on a dime, but the products need to ramp faster.  The whole "end to end" argument is getting stale with a lot of customers  we need to innovate in areas other than revenue and market share or both will ultimately suffer.

Pros: These days mostly just the ability to work from wherever I want to. In theory I like being able to lead the industry with good software and new ideas, but these days cisco doesn't lead much unless you call acquisitions leading. I wonder: did we EVER lead?
Cons: Middle and upper management seems very oblivious. There's no risktaking or anyone wanting to support good ideas whether they pan out or not; that's part of the risk, guys!. As mentioned in other reviews, trying to get anything done from the bottom up is a fool's errand. Actually, I'm not sure there IS a way to get anything done, unless via spinin or acquisition.

Pros: Cisco treats interns well and makes sure they're taken care of with good pay, interesting activities and some free swag.  You get to work in an area of the company that interests you, so you're not just thrown anywhere at random.  How you enjoy the experience will definitely rely on your manager, mentor and team.
Cons: Most of the engineers at Cisco seemed like your stereotypical engineer: working in front of a computer all day without any ability to communicate with normal people.  Definitely a lack of work/life balance, with some engineers working crazy hours without any diversity in their lives.  Not to say that Cisco doesn't have good engineers, but its hard to find one you'd want to sit down and have a beer with.

Pros: Cisco offers a place for people of such diverse backgrounds. I joined later in my career; i hadn't previously worked in IT or for a global corporation but to my surprise, I fitted in. If you are prepared to work hard and are confident enough to come up with ideas, then you are given the opportunity to grow. In recent years I have developed a visual impairment and my Cisco managers have been fantastic at getting me the support I need.
Cons: Over my 10 years at Cisco there has been a lot of reorganisation bringing changes to my role, team, managers. However, the rationale and objectives of the changes are always made clear. We do have to live and work wondering what is coming next.

Pros: Great people to work with.  At times work is challenging. Not so hard to move around between groups. Relentless focus on execution, however, sometime ready, fire, aim. Biggest plus is Flexible work  just get your work done, people don't care where you are That said, some groups do
Cons:
Very big  tiny cog in big machine  hard to make a difference
Constant focus on you adjusting to change  just not changing any of the preyear 2000 systems.
Lots of talk about digitization, but operationally really falling behind  unable to support new business models
Promotions are very hard. Raises and high bonuses are only really given to top performers

Pros: The company culture is good and the Exec/Board always try to do the right think for society. Under the CEO the company is successfully transitioning to a new recurring revenue model, and while there are areas of the business like WebEX that have lost the race with Zoom in this case, Meraki and others are driving the next phase for the company.
Cons: Within the Corporate Real Estate Team there are zero career prospects for males. Females are employed or promoted with little or no experience in corporate real estate, especially within the leadership team. Many males are dissatisfied or even leaving the company for this reason.

Pros:
Ability to learn and grow. Compensation is very good with a combination of base salary and commission. There is a great opportunity to get stock options too.
There is a tremendous amount of web based internal training in every technology.
Also, Cisco has a saying "East your own dog food" meaning they provide you with the tools like cell phone, VPN access from home including a router, Cisco IP phone and video camera.
Cons:
Crazy work schedule. Lots of pressure to perform, sell and drive revenue. Also there is a lot of pressure to do a lot of not core job work like business development, presentations to inernal teams, lots of reports and systems to keep updateded with forecasting, ect...
There is a lack of coordination between hardware sales and services sales.
Often, there is limited time to respond to custmer request albeit SOWs, RFP...

Pros: A great name on you're resume, PTO per year is generous. I kick ass at vlookups now.
Cons: The internal tools dont work well and the process' to get stuff done are long winded and broken. We spend more time fixing errors and wading through BS because things dont work as advertised then actually doing the job itself.  If you spend more time in the beginning doing it right, the whole process gets better, faster, leaner etc... My job could be done with one eye open if tools worked as they should and communication was better.

Pros: So many reasons. Very innovative and expanding into new technologies. Strong focus on collaboration and also making a difference in the world. The culture for the most part reflects this collaborative style but differs a little from group to group. The Executives communicate what is going on within the organization. No layoffs even in a tough economy! Company is very open to people rotating between functional areas and business units although it is on the onus of the individual employee to network and reach out for that next opportunity. Less Bureacracy than I think most other large organizations. Free soda!
Cons: Well, it is a large company so therefore there is some bureacracy. It sometimes takes some time to make decisions in order to go through proper channels. We were forced to take 4 vacation days for the week after Christmas this year whether we wanted to or not or had work to do or not. However, still no layoffs!

Pros:
Great people across the company. Chuck Robbins is a breath of fresh air.

Dominant industry presence, but customers either love Cisco or hate them...not much in between. 

Great package of benefits.
Cons:
Being remote from SJC or RTP can make you invisible. Compensation growth is very limited. 

Sales reporting sucks, making commissions tracking very difficult, and if there's a mistake, good luck getting it corrected. When 'unknown' is the top selling partner in a region, you tend to question all the reporting. 

Politics, politics, politics! If you aren't a suckup, you'll never advance. 

Intense focus on hitting Wall Street expectations for EPS has led to ridiculous T&E budgets. No way to do your job if you are grounded from being front of customers or partners.

Pros: Despite working in a city of more conservative views, which I do not share, Cisco allows me to work in a very equal environment. I do not feel I have same right and my opinions and expertise has equal weight to those of my male colleagues. I feel I can further my career in a same way as my colleagues. flexibility and availability to work from home allows for more balanced worklife schedule and even though I work many hours I do enjoy it and I feel this is m,y choice and not something that has been impose on me. Cisco also encourages women to take technical and managerial positions and we are being rewarded for it.
Cons: So far I have not found any.

Pros:
Good career opportunities
 Work/Life balance is okay
 Good for new joiners and college freshers
 Learning is good
Cons:
Very bad compensation for existing employee 
 Once you are in, you will take years to grow in terms of salary Senior management takes all the budget for them
 After 2 years if you are lucky, you may get 2 to 8% hike. Next hike will come again after 2 years and that too will be the same percentage. 
 New joiners or even college freshers will get almost 50% to 60% higher salary than 6 to 7 years experienced person who is performing well and getting good appreciation. 
 HR making so many rules for compensation or salary normalization but there will be always no budget to implement it.

Pros: In professional IT, there are very few companies who will see you worked at Cisco and wouldn't pay attention to it.  A steady company with welldefined processes, with a clear vision and huge impact on the world. In sales or BU you will see clear results of what you are doing on the market. There is a sense of satisfaction when you enter your bank branch or hospital or hotel or stadium and see Cisco phone on the table or AP on the ceiling : Corporate events are fun and frequent. Great collaboration products let you connect and stay in touch with your remote team around the globe and have a quite dynamic balance of where you work from: home, office or on the go.
Cons: In transformation and future few years will define if the company will exist on the market or not. The road can be bumpy.

Pros:
Cisco is big on diversity. As they hire, they focus on bringing in diverse candidate pools, and 

Occasionally they will give "Day for Me" which is a free day off for the entire company.
Cons:
VERY long hours. Expect to start work early, and be forced to work late with offshore teams. This isn't a once in a while thing, but has become expected with everyone working remotely.

Culture has taken a VERY negative downturn in the past 3 months. Lots of new management changes that highlight how little they care about their employees. There is no support for others. Everything is through the lens of how "I" look to my leaders. 

I would not recommend anyone become a people manager. This role comes with all the blame and none of the reward. You will be expected to constantly push your team for results, work harder with fewer resources, and try to keep spirits up in a team that isn't rewarded for their work.

Pros: Motivated work force, great compensation, strong tools and support to get your job done.   Some of the sharpest folks I've worked with.  Strong customer focus and senior management that does a great job of anticipating market and technology changes all while driving that same market.   Fantastic front line sales engineering staff.   Very good compensation against it's competitors.
Cons:
24x7 work culture and competitive work environment.   Huge product set to keep track of.  Great team environment but with the combination of ambitious lower/mid level management that can take a toll on front line sales teams.   Expectation of doubledigit growth levels despite market conditions, product weaknesses, etc.  

Also...Sales Manager's needing to show 'effort' can mean unnecessary busy work on campaigns that realistically have a slim chance to work.  Sales managers have a very stressful job at Cisco

Pros: Great people and great technologies with lots of energetic team oriented selling.  Lots of great solutions to work with to solve many customer problems, especially over a long term relationship.
Cons: Sales is always full of pressure but there was far too much emphasis on getting the dollars now vs. building a long term relationship with the customers.  You don't call the customer every three hours on month end or quarter end day asking where my PO is?  After a while, customers knew that Cisco only cared about their pockets and only as long as the customer had money to spend.

Pros:
Good location San Jose
 Potential to work on some neat highend and highreliability systems though you might just work on some lame internal tool that shouldn't exist in the first place
 Good, cheap food at cafes
 Free coffee and soda though I heard this changed?
Cons:
Company isn't very efficient. There seemed to be many groups working on the same exact thing. Or, there were groups working on some internal tool which really shouldn't exist since there was an existing solution e.g., open source product.
 Many employees aren't very nice. The small things  not saying hi, for example  add up.
 Lots of needless bureaucracy. There are so many levels of managers and then so many different groups that change all the time.
 Over reliance on contractors.
 Not very diverse.. almost discriminatory in some ways: Everyone in CDO was so very similar.
 Not very innovative

Pros:
Cisco is very good employer  great workplace, great team, great learning opportunities, great compensation packet.  One of the best employers I ever worked for.

My salary increased more than 2 times during 10 years.  I worked in customer support organization Cisco TAC.  

Work options are flexible, it is possible to work from home when necessary.  Also there is some flexibility in choosing work locations depends on position, or working from other company offices worldwide temporarily.

Medical benefits cover the whole family for fulltime regular employees but not for contractors.  Higher grades benefits also include either car allowance, or corporate car.  

Multinational and multicultural environment at work.  All vacations and PTO are respected very carefully, people are not called on vacations.

In case of staff reduction, compensation packet salary for a few month is paid.
Cons:
Getting a promotion grade increase in Cisco is very difficult and very slow.  You need some outstanding achievements beyond your normal work responsibilities to get it.  I got mine after 4 years there.  Not many people got it event after many years of employment.

In customer support organization TAC, you will have pretty narrow and specific area of expertise, knowing only the thing you support and nothing else.  This would cause real difficulties when you want move anywhere from the support even within the company.  Narrow scope of expertise is not demanded in modern world, and you will need to take your own efforts to make it wider, if you want to get another job.

When Cisco thinks it needs staff reduction, it takes it easy.  If specific persons or team are no longer matching current business needs of the company, they are dismissed quickly.

Pros:
Open communication
 Strong Brand
 Trust: as long as you achieve results you can decide what your day will look like 
Being is cisco is really like being in a family 
 Very good benefits
Cons:
Difficult to make a career
 Wage is only ok and it doesn't grow much over the years, even after continued good results
 Sn Mgm often asks to complete useless tasks which is time consuming and forces to work weekend and/or late at night
 Culture slowly fading away and transforming the company to a much less exceptional company
 In the last couple of yrs hypocrisy is becoming the top quality required speaking one thing in company meeting and acting in a totally different way in senior management

Pros:
Pretty flexible about working from home they own Webex
People are smart and overall employees are fun to work with
Meetings are kept to a tolerable minimum
Cons:
Slow to promote or increase salary so you are forced to leave the company if you really want an increases in money and responsibilities.
Like most large corporations, they do not have a mechanism that employees trust to provide feedback about Sr. Managers that will be taken seriously.

Pros: Great sales force, great technology, high visibility within the industry and ability to drive technology and innovation. Lots of customers. If you build a good product, they sell it!.
Cons: Lots of politics. To move up the ladder, need to manage up vs manage down. Passive aggressive culture. Senior management spends lot more time managing up, unaware of the business. Throws money around indiscriminately looking for success. Senior management unaware of what is going on. John Chambers is not connected with reality on the ground. Keeps talking about how great everything is and there are layoffs across the board.

Pros: Good salary for "blue badge" direct employees. Good conditions, autonomy in your work.
Cons: Lot of hot air about diversity and the SJW agenda, and rahrah cultlike atmosphere growing out of control. Diversity of opinions are not welcomed. Layoff culture; continous rounds of large layoffs each time the business dips, which is about every two years, as a standard operating procedure.

Pros: Great vision, Company goals and strategy at the CEO & ELT level
Cons:
Team leads TL lack leadership and self absorbed and stressed to salvage their own jobs not believing in the company goals.at the expense of not following ELT expectations
No process to evaluate TL performance and their bias, subjective choices and effectively lead and support their teams. 
Surveys results are not effective since no change in TL's behaviors for 15 plus years at Cisco Capital just because they are good at Operations and tasks with no previous management experience. Lack of skip level interactions to see through these missed opportunities.

Pros: Culture of decency, intelligence  a place where most of the employee base is collaborative, wellwishing, open and focused on mutual success.
Cons: Transformation today pressures most departments to execute while still figuring out what they should execute, and even as transparency in diminishing relative to past times. Coordinated strategybuilding is difficult with this amount of change, and without more open communication about inthemoment navigation.

Pros:
Flexible work schedule/location unless a manager requires otherwise
 No one on my teams cares whether or not I'm lesbian, and I have never been uncomfortable bringing my wife to a company event. 
 I have never felt as though anything other than my work played a part in my employment or my project/program assignments.
Cons:
Our Talent teams do not actively participate in GLBT+ specific conferences like Lesbians Who Tech for example like we do for other conferences like Grace Hopper Women in Computing for example
 Wish we were more visible in the GLBT+ communities everywhere we have a Cisco site. There should be employee programs and outreach at every site and we should actively participate in community events much more than we do!!

Pros:
A large technology company with a large breadth of technology areas and market coverage should provide varied opportunities for growth
 Great place for people with outstanding technical backgrounds who are looking to be challenged
 Surprising amount of room for growth even though it is currently a large company
Cons:
Challenges exist for people who join and do not have detailed technical skills.  Cisco struggles with how to use and take full advantage of nontechnical resources such as Program Management
 HR processes career and professional development not well managed

Pros: Amazing opportunities to learn different things, technologies, industries. If you enjoy twisting and turning your way through the day and jumping through hoops to make things happen, you'll enjoy Cisco. If you appreciate different challenges and continuous change, you'll enjoy Cisco. If you like consistency and a slower pace, you'll struggle to keep up. If you value leadership and the idea of learning from others as an early in career employee is important to you over pay then you'll enjoy Cisco.
Cons: You won't make a million dollars in your first 10 years ... it might take 20. Pay, and promotional velocity aren't amazing, but you'll never have to worry about getting the things you need.

Pros: Nobody tells you where to draw the line or what not to do, as long as you get the job done. You will have sufficient time to explore any relevant technology and get your hands dirty. Cisco Bangalore has state of the art lab facilities, ample and regular in house training options. From hardware design standpoint, we are given opportunities on par with what happens at San Jose, maybe with a 12Q delay but good work does eventually reach our shores.  The management is transparent top down and recognitions are promptly awarded where due. Pay is on merit and merit is greatly valued with limited scope for internal politics and cronyism. Overall, a great place to be in.
Cons: Sometimes you will doubt hardware's relevance in Cisco's long term 'No.1 IT company' strategy.  Market dynamics change pretty fast, especially in the Service Provider world.

Pros: The environment is respectful of people. Information is openly shared among teams. Management is accessible for conversations even crossfunctionally.  Benefits are good, and internal tech support is very helpful.
Cons: There are significant reorganizations every 3 months for the past 2 years.  With all the upheaval and change in players, projects are delayed and canceled.  No decisions are made.  Everything requires so much crossfunctional alignment and agreement that nothing is ever decided and implemented.  Many projects in my division have been ongoing for several years without real progress...simply reorganizing and renaming initiative something new without business results.  Funding is constantly reduced.  Employees are disillusioned with the lack of traction and completion, and leadership has lost its sense of the competitive marketplace.

Pros: Collaborative, smart, fun people. Work/life balance is respected and encouraged. Changing jobs internally is encouraged and necessary to prevent stagnation. World class benefits. Outstanding high level leadership, middle management less so.
Cons: Too often there are simply too many people on projects and in meetings which hinders ownership, accountability, and progress. While pay is in line with industry and geographic location advancement and compensation increases are very hard to come by which is the nature of such a large organization. You can move around to different roles across the company fairly easily but that doesn't really translate to pay increases or promotions. Global nature of teams and work means meetings will cut into personal time. Company is highly San Jose centric  partly understandable but no less frustrating at times for those in remote locations.

Pros: A solid company that overall treats its employees well.  Good benefits, with ability to work from home every now and then.  A lot of smart and talented people, both in Development and in Supply Chain organizations.  Lots of challenging and interesting projects.  Employee recognition methods are changing for the better.
Cons: For a new product that has not yet "proven" itself in the market, resources are often minimal, so people get spread pretty thin.  The hours can get long for long stretches of time.  The top management can sporadically change direction, and years' worth of work can go down the drain.  Costcutting has led to a lot of churn with contractors and offshoring.

Pros: Flexible work hours and great ability for work/life balance. Excellent benefits and good salary across the board. Generally very good people to work with and good culture that gives back to the community.
Cons: Constant change and lots of politics. Frequent changes to upper management who have little to no regard to those on the team w/deep experience. Many egos and difficult people brought in to lead some groups  and then they lead by bringing in their people and playing favs. Also, you'll find Execs w/little Marketing experience w/big titles. Continued changes to Marketing team w/lots and lots of process. Multiple changes ongoing and about every 3 years the entire model gets shaken up.  Disappointing that Chuck lets this all go on.

Pros:
The people you get to work with here are amazing!!
Also, if you have an idea, all you need to do is to find a few more people who share your passion and just start working on it. You might be surprised where your project might take you. 
Great flexibility around where you are working from and when you do your work. 
Access to technology is great.
And Cisco is amazing at giving back to the community, really proud of what we can achieve together.
Cons: Occasionally you might take work home and after all it's a huge organisation to navigate. You have to work for your development and in some parts of the organisation a straight career ladder is not available.

Pros: Flexibility, Working with other smart people, stable company, caring company, opportunities to learn new things, opportunity to move around to get broader business experience, good benefits  especially the 401k matching, tuition reimbursement, work for an industry leader and visionary, great brand,
Cons: if you don't set your boundaries this place will take everything you are willing to give it, increasing costs of medical benefits, not enough training and expectations for people managers in regards to their people management skills.

Pros: I am surrounded by smart people who are well intentioned. People feel like, not only are we doing good work here, but we are also doing something that has the potential to change the way people connect.  Innovating new ways to to interact with each other and our world is exciting.  Changing business models and being part of what's next is a great thing. I like coming to work almost every day.
Cons: The campus environment is dated  WAY DATED!  It doesn't scream "CHANGE THE WORLD BY CREATING"  it's more Dilbertesque.  Also, you have to be able to navigate a lot of ambiguity and be self directed or this place will be overwhelming.

Pros: very flexible on work time, good compensation for onCall, nice office
Cons: micro management, too much management involvement & dictation in technical decisions and daily work, not properly included into Cisco always felt like an forgotten outpost, resilient against industry standard technologies & methods & systems, patching stupid & fundamentally broken systems instead of replacing them with proper ones, too much oncall, local management had no say or information on what upper management is doing or deciding, Cisco treating people and contractors really bad when the earnings call is around the corner, not using external services and providers but trying to build inhouse and fail hard, being a miserable open source citizen, not giving resources for proper testing & automation

Pros: Cisco is growing! There are a wide range of career opportunities for motivated workers.  They encourage employees to continuously learn and add to their skills. They recognize achievements fairly and promote based on accomplishments.  It is a fast paced environment where team work is cherished. There are no boundaries and innovation is sacred.  Your input will be valued if it is valuable. You can live your dreams at Cisco
Cons: It is a very large company. Rather than consentrating on being a superstar you must concentrate on being an outstanding team member. You are measured on the value you bring to the project, team, organization and most importantly the customer. This may be more difficult for people who tend to do better solo.

Pros: large company, lots of different oppertunities.  you can go into cisco as a nobody and leave as a professional networking guy with 5 cisco certs under your belt.  you have to take advantage of the situation.
Cons: in the group i worked in, no work life balance, all work.  ive heard thats not normal for cisco though.  with the group i was in it wasnt the persuit of knowledge, it was the pursuit of getting it done. i would try to understand more about how things worked but would often get back the response from someone of "i dont know, why do you care"

Pros:
1.  Competitive salaries and benefits.
2.  Lots of elearning opportunities, and you can study any area you want.
3.  Very open and communicative corporate cultureyou can always find out about other business units and their strategies.
4.  Collaborative, teambased environment
5.  Great internal IT resources and support, including latest videoconferencing and webinar tools
Cons:
1.  Lots of pressure to keep up with latest trendsyou can't coast at Cisco.
2.  There are still internal power struggles and individuals can still wreak havoc with their teams and employees.
3.  Long hours
4.  Poor internal HR support
5.  Almost no admin supportyou have to learn to do everything yourself

Pros: Fair salary and compensation. Nice to have option to work from home.
Cons: Some of the most  arrogant and ill trained managers in the industry. The idea of managers at Cisco is if you are a skilled NCE, you are a good manager. Managers are empowered to do everything right or wrong and they have the practice of hiring very young managers who may have excelled in the field. The management style is like in the army, generals talk to generals and no one cares or listens otherwise. Emails never get responded and no one listens to voicemail. One of the most arrogant companies to work for and it takes months or years to implement a program

Pros:
Working at Cisco, especially now, is pretty fun.  It has been a fastpaced and contently changing environment for years but in just the last thirty months the tempo has increased. Everyone seems more focused and better aligned as the company. This is as the company transitions to a more "business outcomes" mindset  from selling "eyeglasses" to selling "better vision".  

But you must be able to reinvent yourself with some frequency and deal with change.

I do not think there has been a better time to be at Cisco than right now.
Cons: Opportunities must be sought out.  Compensation seems to lag "valley" benchmarks for nonexecutive level employees. Work/life balance sometimes gets akimbo. Frugality sometimes hamstrings success.

Pros: I was a summer intern in the supply chain and I had a fantastic time! Great coworkers who were always willing to help, fun perks, competitive salary, and a realworld look at what industry is like. The people I worked with really made me feel appreciated too, and that was a huge plus.
Cons: While I got good experience and lots to talk about in interviews, I don't know how much my work actually helped the company. Near the end of my internship I got the feeling that the interns from the year before had done the exact same projects we were assigned to do, making it almost feel like our time was wasted. I wish our projects had more of an impact on the company.

Pros: Allow you to select Macs as your computer to use.  Good bonuses and salary.  Competitive benefits. Nice facilities to work in.
Cons: Upper management is destroying the company by having no clue to where they are going or what business they are in.  Cisco's future is unfortunately to become like HP where engineering is nearly absent and the products are very subpar.

Pros: Cisco has the resources to do anything they want.  If they want to fix a problem they can.  The saying at Cisco is, there are jobs.. just not a lot of good ones.
Cons: The last 20 years created a huge outsourcing black hole, and along with that many engineers were brought into the US to support customers here and abroad.  Unfortunately they don't speak English very well, and many are completely unintelligible.  Some of the managers are also from India and don't want to remove these folks, and so the work gets piled onto the US engineers to make up for them.. so you'll become their mule.

Pros: Job Rotation is the only reason why I've been here for 18 years! Once you master your roleusually in 34 years, then you can rotate to a new role where you can take on more responsibility and learn new skills. This has allowed me to take new roles without changing companies and I've been able to carry over things like equity, PTO, etc.
Cons: In the past I've taken some parallel positions just to learn something new. It may be that If I had stayed in  a role for a longer tenure then maybe I would have been promoted fasterbut who knows.

Pros: Lots of smart people. The overall quality of talent is excellent, and there is a strong vibe of a demand for excellence.  The company is willing to change tacks, and quite quickly, which is important in today's world, and impressive for a company of its size.
Cons:
As much time is spent on staking out and maintaining one's "territory" as on actually working. Most inquiries to other dept's for assistance/cooperation are treated as threats and much effort is put into attempting to eviscerate or eliminate those that seem to provide a threat to one's territory.  Creates a pretty unproductive working environment.
Bureacracy re: policies, procedures, etc. is extremely thick and not streamlined.

Pros: Innovative company for networking industry.  Continuous learning opportunity for both technical and leadership skills.  Excellent culture in giving back to community.  All employees are allowed to spend upto 5 days paid time off to give back to community as volunteer.  Cisco is the industry leaders in multiple areas in Routing/Switching/Server/Data Center.  Very stable company.  Lots of learning opportunities as company encourage to rotate the job functions within the company.  And great benefits including 4 weeks of paid PTOs can be used for vacation or sick leave.
Cons: Company is big and sometimes it took long time to make a decision.  Process oriented company and it can be rigid sometimes.  Sometimes it can be good.  Sometime it can play as downside.  Other than that, Cisco is a great company to work and learn.

Pros: Flexibility, dedication to customers, mission, potential to impact the world
Cons: Toooooo many reorgs, politics decide who gets promoted, a lot of bad mid and senior level managers who have zero ability to lead, serious ageism pushing senior talent out to make room for new recruits. Also too much fat in the org too many people doing too much overlapping work that don't necessarily move the business.

Pros: With Cisco for longer than a decade, can tell you that Cisco Corporation is absolutely the best corporation to work for  extraordinary people with great culture, and a winning mindset. ELT executive leadership is strong leaders with courage and vision, more importantly are amazing human beings.
Cons: Watch out for poorly run Business Units. Loyalty has zero value in Cisco. Declining business unit will cut people. And once laidoff, even if your skills and expertise match or exceed internal open openings, you are out of luck. Hope Cisco realizes and improve this aspect.

Pros: This is a very good company to work for as far as large corporations go. People are generally treated with respect although there are always exceptions and the culture is nice  teamwork oriented, etc. The benefits are pretty good.
Cons: No regular raises since 2001  it is possible to get "equity adjustments" but very difficult. Even top performers tend to go a year or two between these "adjustments." In terms of salary, loyalty is not rewarded  it is very common for Cisco to hire externally at higher pay grades than the internal people who have been there for a long time  and the external hires do not necessarily have more experience overall.

Pros:
Cisco is employee and customer focused
 this has been brought our even more so in the pandemic with SLT regular checkins, commitment to staff, commitment to customers, flexibility for customers and encouragement for staff to get involved in local causes to help.
 approachable management with clear direction
 flexible working was supported prior to the pandemic but even more so during and expected to be after
 employee wealthfare is pivotal and programs support this
 relevant technology but delivered with a focus on the customer outcomes and how that technology enables, not simply about selling "a widget"
 lines of accountability and responsibility
 opportunity to progress
Cons: the IT industry is one of constant change, driven by customer demand and technology  Cisco has to change and mould to be aligned, so to some respects change is a constant

Pros:
Excellent work environment, casual but demanding
 The Cisco name:  the king of networking
 A very solid, stable company, without any really aggressive competition
 Plenty of paid time off
Cons:
As an intern, I have observed that the work week can be extremely long for full time employees, and this type of time commitment is expected when customer issues arise some members of my team just put in a 100 hour work week
 There is some flexibility with work/life balance in that you can work a 40hour week if you get your job done and can choose when you come to work and leave, but if you expect any type of promotion, work must be your life
 Too many constraints and stringent processes causes a lack of innovation and creativity

Pros:

Pros: Big Bucks in the bank insulate this company from A LOT of mistakes. Cisco has great benefits,  a nine to five culture, very good pay, excellent market share, nice buildings, employees are generally empowered to do stuff unless it's innovative  see below
Cons: Absolutely no career growth unless you want to move to India. No ability to cross over business units or get into new technologies, very static environment. Cisco generally hates people who innovate because that activity is inherently risky. If Cisco wants innovation it will go out an buy it! Mike Volpe once said that Cisco didn't need to do R&D because the whole of Silicon Valley was it's R&D lab.

Pros: Having a job there led to a much better role at a better company…
Cons:
I worked at Cisco leading one of the AR teams, and I have to say that this was THE worst culture I have been part of. I had nightmares about the role after quitting for about six months, and every time I had to speak with my toxic director manager, I would have heart palpations starting the night before because she was absolutely awful. There is a micro culture of submission on the Comms team because anyone who disagreed with anything was pushed out. I wouldn’t recommend Cisco to anyone.

Plus they lowballed me in the leader role I was given by offering me exactly what I made in the position I left for Cisco, but they finally “relented” and offered me 1k more to lead a team. Pffft

Pros: The environment within the sales dept is very collaborative and almost everyone is willing to offer advice when asked. Promotions are about who you know but good work performance is still recognized and called out. If you don't work and only do the bare minimum then it will take alot longer to get promoted and recognized amongst such a large company.
Cons: The beaurocracy and red tape makes it extremely difficult to voice an opinion about an oncoming change. Management listens but makes very little change unless its complaints from a large majority. Very metric based company. Company seems to constantly be undergoing some sort of small or large reorg but from what I've seen, very little downsizing has happened.

Pros: Great benefits, can't complain about pay and progression. Always treated well and rewarded adequately for good work.
Cons: Large fiefdoms in the company, with highmid/upper management always focusing on improving careers. Have to leave company and work at startups to do any real innovation that requires risk.

Pros:

Pros: Really interesting work. Good work life balance, depending on your current project and how much you worry about securing a system in the time you're given. Surprised at the group we've been able to hire and mostly keep. Smart, hard working coworkers you will always be learning from.
Cons:
Cisco doesn't give our group enough budget for promotions or raises to retain people. Talks a lot about how awesome we are, how appreciated our work is, fails to prove that.

Trusted to take on more and more responsibility but not good enough for promotion. Less and less time to look at more and more complex projects, while being expected to offer more help to the groups we work with and do more secondary tasks.

Pros:
Company overall does amazing things for communities around them, the environment and social justice. Also provide employees the ability to engage and contribute here.
Good opportunity for internal movement, advancement not as much.
There are A LOT of great people here, and learning new things on a daily basis is constant and rewarding.
Cons: Recent leadership changes have affected culture. There are many areas of the business where driving outcomes is done at expense of the people/team members. Decision making is becoming much less transparent. Favorites are protected and enabled.

Pros:
Great People to work with who are very knowledgable about technology, business processes and back office systems.

Cisco is supportive of it's employees learning new things, and in some instances will even pay a portion of the fees associated in obtaining an advanced degree.

Cisco provides more flexibility in working from home or in the office than any other company I know of.
Cons:
Promotions are few and opportunities for advancement are limited.  

Compensation doesn't keep pace with promotions, I know of people promoted to director who received fairly limited pay increases.

Additionally I recently hired someone and was apalled by the level of compensation they receive compared to peers.

Pros: One of the best ''schools'' in the world for new technologies. It was like a river of knowledge that just kept on flowing and flowing, and would never run dry.
Cons: Some people feel frustrated when they see you succeed and get better results than them. So they will do all they can do make your life miserable, including bullying you and say all sorts of lies to get others to dislike you as well. It takes a lot of strength of character to handle that and come away with your Dignity intact, but it's possible, because I did it.

Pros:
I started at Cisco through the awardwinning Cisco Sales Associates Program CSAP and the amount of investment that Cisco put in to transform us into Ciscograde engineers was unbelievable. There is always help around the corner only if you remember to ask!

As an Associate Systems Engineer, I was trained on Cisco's vast portfolio including Enterprise, Security, Data Center and Collaboration tools. We were encouraged to complete CCNA and CCNP certifications.

The worklife balance is probably the best thing about Cisco, next only to it's multicultural workforce. 

Shoutout again to CSAP that makes Cisco one of the best places to start your career at.
Cons: Leadership changes mean changes in the goals we're trying to achieve but in a dynamic industry like ours, I believe that's a necessity.

Pros: Cisco has not given up yet. There are enough experienced people to know how to get through tough times. Cisco has a solid run rate that could last them 20 years, key will be to keep the long view, like they had in the 90s
Cons: There is no top down leadership any longer. There has been a culture of consensus that anyone can say no but no one is able to make a decision. There is little to no upward mobility due to the hangeroners that believe that selling boxes is the only way. The engineering is right Cisco foundation has been lost.

Pros:
Flexible working hours with great worklife balance
Work from home option is one of the biggest facility this company provides and there is hardly any micro management
Cons:
Hard to manage work life balance
Very big company with constant changes

Pros: Good Salary, great bonus if you are Tech Lead or higher, benefits are okay.
Cons: Employees and management are very risk adverse and innovation is not commonplace.

Pros: Fast paced.  Challenging.  Most finance people are very intelligent, knowledgeable and highly professional.  Teams typically are very collaborative and work to help all succeed.
Cons:
You never know when Cisco will outsource your job, downsize or exit your business.  So all constantly worry when their last day will be.

Very little investment in training finance people.  Internal job rotation program is not actively managed well so movement is slow as people are afraid to change jobs for fear to lose their job.

Finance teams are a reporting function to enable management by numbers.  Finance organization needs to really and truly be value add to their business partners rather than managing their business partners like Monday morning quarterbacks.

Pros: Cisco has long been the standard for great technology companies to work for and I've loved my jobs at Cisco for quite some time. Competitive compensation, benefits, and semiannual bonus potential as well as good mobility and career path opportunities. The management and leadership culture puts priority on their people and in my experience at least, is very supportive.
Cons:
1. Not as many fun company events as there used to be, but it's all part of evolving priorities of a large company feeling the need to be socially responsible.
2. Like with any large publicly traded company, there are periodic restructurings layoffs as the whims of Wallstreet impact the business.

Pros: Knowledge sharing is key.  Everyone is open to help out.  It is great in this industry to have access to the origin of new technologies and get your hands on anything you need.
Cons: As the company grows, cisco culture is being lost.  I am happy here though, the grass isn't always greener on the other side.

Pros: If anyone wants to accelerate their career, you need not look elsewhere. CSAP is one of the most rewarding experiences I've ever had. It's tough because they expect a lot from you, but if you do your job and work hard you will be just fine. CSAP was like college all over again for me! You meet so many young professionals and hop in to those same sales/technology classes based on your track engineer or sales representative. I went through the engineer track and got put into customer role plays, shadowing opportunities with field teams, passing required exams, and half a year of classes. I've learned so much from all my mentors and peers, and these learned traits will stick with me for the rest of my life!
Cons: None! Be ready to study!

Pros: Highly dynamic, collaborative company. Depending upon which org and leadership one is under there are great opportunities to have your voice heard and help shape direction. Lots of opportunity and resources to evolve skills.
Cons: With being agile and dynamic there's often questions about direction and how to measure success. Many layers of specialists due to complexity of portfolio.

Pros: The benefits are good, the ability to work from home considering much of work is accomplished in conference calls / WebEx sessions is a nice plus, some of the newer offices are nice. Compensation is good. Work/life balance is pretty decent work from home, using devices to connect. Gym and medical center at the San Jose campus is very nice and is a great perk for local employees.
Cons: Hypercompetitive environment encourages bad business behavior and investment choices. Insular and nepotistic management at senior levels. Cultlike 'love' of the CEO. Cafes are pretty good, but prices are high. Free snacks / drinks eliminated in costcutting back in 2009 could save more cost by not rewarding the underperforming senior management :.

Pros: Great company and full of talented people.  Great compensation and benefits.  Everyone loves John Chambers and Gary Moore and SVP management is solid.  Hard working but well rewarding.
Cons: It's getting to be a large company so politics are pretty much a part of the business.  Starting to lose the difference between perception of and getting actual work done.  Repeated layoffs have demoralized the employees.  The company is going through the biggest transformation and it will be interesting to see if they succeed.

Job Title: Financial Analyst In The Lift Program
Pros: Cisco is a great company to work for. The company provides numerous opportunities to learn and grow. I have thoroughly enjoyed my time in the LiFT Leaders In Finance and Tech Program as well. This program pushes me to reach my full potential,has introduced me to a variety of people, and has provided me the opportunity to have rotations in both finance and accounting. I can't imagine working for another company other than Cisco.
Cons: Honestly, I can't think of any major cons of the company or the program. Granted, I have had to work with some difficult people in the past, but that is the case with all companies, and if anything, has taught me how to work with a variety of people.

Pros: Offered good experience in SaaS software.
Cons: Top and next level management at WebEx are clueless.  They bounce back and forth like a pingpong ball.  They are unable to develop and execute cohesive product roadmaps, yet they fool themselves into believing they can.  Employees are discouraged from bringing up "sensitive issues" to management.  Employees are encouraged to "not rock the boat."  Marketing department is unable to commit to project deadlines, yet blame this on others all the time.  Take responsibility for making things happen?  That's not a Cisco WebEx strongpoint.

Pros: Cisco was a great place to work. Too many perks to list. Leadership generally lived by the core principles of the Cisco "People Deal", an initiative to retain talent by putting the needs of employees first. One example  I was supported through a very difficult and extended personal leave. Cisco retained my job and welcomed me back once the crisis was past.
Cons: Engineeringdriven company with scattered UX practice and greatly varying levels of success. There are pockets of great design in various BUs, but unfortunately I was not in one of them. 8 bosses in 5 years, and the only excellent and fully competent one I had was fired because she rubbed some oldtimers the wrong way.

Pros: a good place to start a career, learn a lot in a short time. Company well managed with the pandemic. Mandatory working from home.
Cons:
High rotation between engineers, managers, PMs, plus layoffs every 6months then rehiring... Difficult to change internally position. Need to know with whom to be a friend in order to get a promotion. Everything depends on visibility how popular you are. Lack of transparency. Heard plenty of internal issues with managers: emotional distress, inequality. Employees afraid of talking about it loudly. Officially we were told to care of ourselves but due to the lack of a workforce, everyone is overloaded. Some managers don't allow to register overtime. So, you might land working 50h per week. 
Foreigners do not stay long, due to cultaral maching with Polish work culture.

Pros: I joined Cisco in 1995 and left in 2014.  The company I joined was not the company I left.  The culture of family existed in the 1990's and early 2000's.  The products, technologies, and people were fantastic and still are very good.
Cons: Cisco now does what large companies do, which is annual layoffs.  Sometimes these layoffs are actually ongoing just aren't reported as they are below 3% of the total employee population.  This systemic issue leads to a culture of CYA and backstabbing, especially at executive levels.

Pros:
Checking all the boxes related to social justice and D & I
Chuck is a great face for the company
Cons:
NO clear strategy that is executed with any priority/investment commitment 
Multiple layoffs due to lack of portfolio and wfp
Little career/promo opportunity if you aren't part of the 'deck' that continues to get shuffled at the top
EXTREMELY slow

Pros: The attitude of "customer success" is very prevalent within the company, so if you run up against a roadblock, using that magic phrase opens many doors.
Cons: In Customer Advocacy, there were no real opportunities for advancement unless you were willing to relocate to San Jose.  Benefit costs increased substantially every year, but there were no raises to be had.  Reorganization happened every 6 months, so I never had the same boss for one full review cycle.  Management was constantly trying to justify the existence of our group by adding supplemental job tasks to the job description, but failing to recognize and evangelize the inherent value of our core deliverables.

Pros: Great culture, great security, very smart people. It's a high integrity company with high integrity people. Very peoplefriendly place to work.
Cons: Neverending reorganizations make it extremely difficult to get anything done. Lots of decisions seem to be made based on politics and personal favors, and those decisions don't last. The result is lack of trust w/ the most executive leadership.

Pros: The best Cisco offers is flexibility in working hours.  Lots of options in when and where to work from.  Home and different locations.  Other benefits aren't the best but are acceptable.
Cons: Downside is the flexibility in working hours can sometime end up causing you to work extra long hours especially when under a time crunch.  Cisco has a fully outsourced manufacturing.  As such, many of the manufacturing operation has long since moved to lower cost regions.  This resulted in the need to work odd hours considering that time zone differences.  This can at times be a strain when new products are being launched.

Pros: An ambitious company with its heart in the right place. Capable of producing incredible technology. Pay and conditions are excellent and you get the sense that you work for a company that is not out to screw its employees. Company has a very high reputation that is, in my opinion, well deserved.
Cons: Despite working for a networking company, communication between functions can leave a lot to be desired. Company is known for being inflexible towards its customers. The overall strategy and direction can sometimes come across as being a little vague.

Pros: Challenging work which contributes to a lot of learning and growing as an employee and as a person.  Working there twenty years ago when the business was booming, was a fantastic, one time life experience.  There are a lot of smart people at Cisco, which was a great environment to work in.
Cons: They lost focus of the most important asset, people.  It is a very top and bottom organization/company.  The executive compensation gap compared to 55% of the company, is HUGE.  There should have been more key leadership changes at the very top, much much much sooner and often.

Pros:
Transparent leadership decision making
The best technology in the world
Fantastic work experience, from offices to how they equip you remotely
Focus on YOU as an employee, not what you do in a current role
High ability to move around, try new things and grow new skills
Every employee has a voice, and it is listened to
Working with the smartest, talented team in the world, around the world
